options.text: Create a temporary username and password for the temporary partner team members. Auto-clean the usernames and passwords after the work engagement has ended.
Create a workforce identity pool and federate the identity pool with the identity provider (IdP) of the temporary partner team.
Implement just-in-time privileged access to Google Cloud for the temporary partner team.
Add the identities of the temporary partner team members to your identity provider (IdP).

questions.explanation:
Workforce Identity Federation lets external workforce users—including partners and contractors—authenticate through their existing identity provider and receive IAM-authorized access to Google Cloud resources. A workforce identity pool federated with the partner’s IdP keeps identity lifecycle control with that employer, so users removed from the IdP can no longer authenticate for access. [Workforce Identity Federation](https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/workforce-identity-federation)

**Learn more:** [Workforce Identity Federation](https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/workforce-identity-federation)

Your security team wants to lower the risk that user-managed keys are mishandled or compromised. To do this, you must stop developers from creating user-managed service account keys for projects in their organization. How should this be enforced?

options.text: Configure Secret Manager to manage service account keys.
Enable an organization policy to disable service accounts from being created.
Enable an organization policy to prevent service account keys from being created.
Remove the iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken permission from users.

questions.explanation:
Enforce the Organization Policy constraint that disables service account key creation (`iam.managed.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation`, or the legacy `iam.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation`). The policy blocks creation of new external, user-managed service account keys in the projects where it applies, reducing the risk from unmanaged long-lived credentials.

**Learn more:** [Restrict IAM service account usage | Organization Policy](https://docs.cloud.google.com/organization-policy/restrict-service-accounts) · [Create and delete service account keys](https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/keys-create-delete)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization uses Vertex AI Workbench Instances. You must ensure that newly deployed Instances are automatically kept current and that users cannot inadvertently change operating-system settings. What should you do?

options.text: Enforce the disableRootAccesa and requireAutoUpgradeSchedule organization policies for newly deployed Instances.
Enable the VM Manager and ensure the corresponding Google Compute Engine instances are added.
Implement a firewall rule that prevents Secure Shell access to the corresponding Google Compute Engine instances by using tags.
Assign the AI Notebooks Runner and AI Notebooks Viewer roles to the users of the AI Workbench Instances.

questions.explanation:
Enforcing the Vertex AI Workbench organization policies for automatic scheduled upgrades and disabled root access requires newly created instances to have an automatic upgrade schedule and prevents them from enabling root access. This keeps the environment updated while preventing users from altering operating-system settings with root privileges.

**Learn more:** [Organization policy constraints | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/organization-policy/reference/org-policy-constraints)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work for a multinational organization with systems deployed across multiple cloud providers, including Google Cloud. Your organization operates an extensive on-premises security information and event management (SIEM) system. New security-compliance regulations require relevant Google Cloud logs to be seamlessly integrated with the existing SIEM, providing a unified view of security events.  
  
You need to implement a solution that exports Google Cloud logs to the on-premises SIEM using a push-based, near-real-time approach. You must prioritize fault tolerance, security, and autoscaling capabilities. In particular, you must ensure that logs are resent if a log delivery fails. What should you do?

options.text: Create a Pub/Sub topic for log aggregation. Write a custom Python script on a Cloud Function Leverage the Cloud Logging API to periodically pull logs from Google Cloud and forward the logs to the SIEM. Schedule the Cloud Function to run twice per day.

Collect all logs into an organization-level aggregated log sink and send the logs to a Pub/Sub topic. Implement a primary Dataflow pipeline that consumes logs from this Pub/Sub topic and delivers the logs to the SIEM. Implement a secondary Dataflow pipeline that replays failed messages.

Deploy a Cloud Logging sink with a filter that routes all logs directly to a syslog endpoint. The endpoint is based on a single Compute Engine hosted on Google Cloud that routes all logs to the on-premises SIEM. Implement a Cloud Function that triggers a retry action in case of failure.
Utilize custom firewall rules to allow your SIEM to directly query Google Cloud logs. Implement a Cloud Function that notifies the SIEM of a failed delivery and triggers a retry action.

questions.explanation:
An organization-level aggregated Cloud Logging sink can route relevant logs across the organization to a Pub/Sub topic in near real time. Pub/Sub supports redelivery when a subscriber does not acknowledge a message, while a Dataflow streaming pipeline provides managed, autoscaling processing to deliver the records to the SIEM. A secondary replay mechanism preserves recovery from failed deliveries.

**Learn more:** [Route logs to supported destinations](https://docs.cloud.google.com/logging/docs/export/configure_export_v2) · [Subscription retry policy](https://docs.cloud.google.com/pubsub/docs/subscription-retry-policy)

Your organization is moving to Google Cloud. You need to ensure that only trusted container images are deployed to Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) clusters in a project. Containers must be deployed from a centrally managed Container Registry and be signed by a trusted authority.  
  
What should you do? (Choose two.)

options.text: Enable Container Threat Detection in the Security Command Center (SCC) for the project.
Configure the trusted image organization policy constraint for the project.
Create a custom organization policy constraint to enforce Binary Authorization for Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE).
Enable PodSecurity standards, and set them to Restricted.
Configure the Binary Authorization policy with respective attestations for the project.

questions.explanation:
The trusted image organization policy constraint restricts deployments to approved container image registries. A Binary Authorization policy that requires attestations enforces that an image was signed and approved by the configured trusted authority before GKE permits deployment.

**Learn more:** [Binary Authorization overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/binary-authorization/docs/overview) · [Binary Authorization key concepts](https://docs.cloud.google.com/binary-authorization/docs/key-concepts)

You are directing all internet-facing traffic from Google Cloud through your on-premises internet connection. You want to achieve this securely while providing the highest possible bandwidth.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Create an HA VPN connection to Google Cloud. Replace the default 0.0.0.0/0 route.
Create a routing VM in Compute Engine. Configure the default route with the VM as the next hop.
Configure Cloud Interconnect with HA VPN. Replace the default 0.0.0.0/0 route to an on-premises destination.
Configure Cloud Interconnect and route traffic through an on-premises firewall.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Interconnect supplies private, scalable, high-bandwidth connectivity between a VPC network and an on-premises network. Sending the traffic through an on-premises firewall before it uses the on-premises internet connection applies centralized security controls, while avoiding the substantially lower per-tunnel bandwidth of HA VPN.

**Learn more:** [Cloud Interconnect overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/network-connectivity/docs/interconnect/concepts/overview) · [Cloud VPN overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/network-connectivity/docs/vpn/concepts/overview)

You are diagnosing access-denied errors between Compute Engine instances connected to a Shared VPC and BigQuery datasets. The datasets are in a project protected by a VPC Service Controls perimeter. What should you do?

options.text: Add the host project containing the Shared VPC to the service perimeter.
Add the service project where the Compute Engine instances reside to the service perimeter.
Create a service perimeter between the service project where the Compute Engine instances reside and the host project that contains the Shared VPC.
Create a perimeter bridge between the service project where the Compute Engine instances reside and the perimeter that contains the protected BigQuery datasets.

questions.explanation:
For Shared VPC, VPC Service Controls requires the host project to be included in the same service perimeter as the Shared VPC service projects. Requests from Compute Engine instances use the Shared VPC network owned by the host project, so omitting that host project causes access to protected BigQuery datasets to be denied.

**Learn more:** [Service perimeter details and configuration — VPC Service Controls](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vpc-service-controls/docs/service-perimeters) · [Protecting resources with VPC Service Controls — Compute Engine](https://docs.cloud.google.com/compute/docs/instances/protecting-resources-vpc-service-controls)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have a highly sensitive BigQuery workload containing personally identifiable information (PII), and you need to ensure it cannot be accessed from the internet. To prevent data exfiltration, only requests originating from authorized IP addresses may query your BigQuery tables.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Use service perimeter and create an access level based on the authorized source IP address as the condition.
Use Google Cloud Armor security policies defining an allowlist of authorized IP addresses at the global HTTPS load balancer.
Use the Restrict Resource Service Usage organization policy constraint along with Cloud Data Loss Prevention (DLP).
Use the Restrict allowed Google Cloud APIs and services organization policy constraint along with Cloud Data Loss Prevention (DLP).

questions.explanation:
VPC Service Controls can protect BigQuery with a service perimeter to mitigate data-exfiltration risk. An Access Context Manager access level can classify requests by source IP address; applying that access level to the perimeter permits access from the authorized IP ranges while blocking other internet-originated requests.

**Learn more:** [VPC Service Controls for BigQuery](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/vpc-sc) · [Allow access to protected resources from outside a perimeter](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vpc-service-controls/docs/use-access-levels)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company’s Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) establishes a requirement that business data be stored in specified locations because regulatory requirements affect the company’s global-expansion plans. After working through the implementation details for this requirement, you determine the following:  
  
- The services in scope are covered by the Google Cloud Data Residency Terms.  
- The business data remains in specific locations within the same organization.  
- The folder structure can include multiple data-residency locations.  
  
You plan to use the Resource Location Restriction organization policy constraint. At which level of the resource hierarchy should you configure the constraint?

options.text: Folder
Resource
Project
Organization

questions.explanation:
Organization policies, including the Resource Location Restriction constraint, can be set at the organization, folder, or project level and apply to child resources. A folder-level policy allows separate branches of one organization to enforce different permitted locations, supporting multiple data-residency locations while governing the projects and resources within each branch.

**Learn more:** [Restrict resource locations | Organization Policy | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/organization-policy/restrict-locations) · [Data residency | Assured Workloads | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/assured-workloads/docs/data-residency)

A retail customer lets users upload comments and product reviews. The customer needs to ensure the text contains no sensitive data before the comments or reviews are published.  
  
Which Google Cloud service should be used to accomplish this?

options.text: Cloud Key Management Service
Cloud Data Loss Prevention API
BigQuery
Web Security Scanner

questions.explanation:
Cloud Data Loss Prevention API, now part of Sensitive Data Protection, inspects text for sensitive information using infoType detectors and can de-identify or redact detected content before it is published.\
\
**Learn more:** [Inspect sensitive text by using the DLP API](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sensitive-data-protection/docs/inspect-sensitive-text-api) · [De-identifying sensitive data](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sensitive-data-protection/docs/deidentify-sensitive-data)

Create a Folder per department under the Organization. For each department's Folder, assign the Project Browser role to the Google Group related to that department.
Create a Project per department under the Organization. For each department's Project, assign the Project Viewer role to the Google Group related to that department.
Create a Project per department under the Organization. For each department's Project, assign the Project Browser role to the Google Group related to that department.

questions.explanation:
IAM roles granted on a folder are inherited by all projects and resources within that folder. Assigning the department Google Group the Project Viewer role on its department folder therefore gives the group read-only access to resources in all current and future projects placed in that folder. The Project Browser role only permits browsing the resource hierarchy and does not grant access to project resources.

**Learn more:** [About resource hierarchy](https://cloud.google.com/resource-manager/docs/cloud-platform-resource-hierarchy) · [Browser roles and permissions](https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/roles-permissions/browser)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization uses Active Directory and wants to configure Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML). You must configure and enforce single sign-on (SSO) for every user.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: 1. Create a new SAML profile.2. Populate the sign-in and sign-out page URLs.3. Upload the X.509 certificate.4. Configure Entity ID and ACS URL in your IdP.

1. Configure prerequisites for OpenID Connect (OIDC) in your Active Directory (AD) tenant.2. Verify the AD domain.3. Decide which users should use SAML.4. Assign the pre-configured profile to the select organizational units (OUs) and groups.
1. Create a new SAML profile.2. Upload the X.509 certificate.3. Enable the change password URL.4. Configure Entity ID and ACS URL in your IdP.
1. Manage SAML profile assignments.2. Enable OpenID Connect (OIDC) in your Active Directory (AD) tenant.3. Verify the domain.

questions.explanation:
SAML SSO requires a SAML profile containing the identity provider’s sign-in and sign-out URLs and verification certificate. The service provider’s Entity ID and Assertion Consumer Service (ACS) URL must also be configured in the identity provider so it can issue assertions to the correct recipient endpoint. OpenID Connect configuration is a different federation protocol and does not satisfy a SAML requirement.

**Learn more:** [Microsoft Entra ID user provisioning and single sign-on](https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/identity/federating-gcp-with-azure-ad-configuring-provisioning-and-single-sign-on)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization is building a sophisticated machine learning (ML) model that predicts customer behavior for targeted marketing campaigns. The BigQuery dataset used for training contains sensitive personal information. You must design security controls for the AI/ML pipeline. Data privacy must be preserved throughout the model’s lifecycle, and personal data must not be used during training. You must also limit dataset access to only an authorized subset of people. What should you do?

options.text: De-identify sensitive data before model training by using Cloud Data Loss Prevention (DLP)APIs. and implement strict Identity and Access Management (IAM) policies to control access to BigQuery.
Implement Identity-Aware Proxy to enforce context-aware access to BigQuery and models based on user identity and device.
Implement at-rest encryption by using customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK) for the pipeline. Implement strict Identity and Access Management (IAM) policies to control access to BigQuery.
Deploy the model on Confidential VMs for enhanced protection of data and code while in use. Implement strict Identity and Access Management (IAM) policies to control access to BigQuery.

questions.explanation:
De-identifying sensitive fields before training prevents personal data from being used by the model while retaining usable data for analysis. Cloud DLP, now part of Sensitive Data Protection, supports discovery and de-identification of sensitive BigQuery data. BigQuery IAM enables granular, least-privilege access so only authorized users can access the dataset.

**Learn more:** [Using Sensitive Data Protection with BigQuery](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sensitive-data-protection/docs/dlp-bigquery) · [Introduction to security and access controls in BigQuery](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/access-control-intro)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are backing up application logs to a shared Cloud Storage bucket that both the administrator and analysts can access. Analysts must not be able to access logs containing any personally identifiable information (PII). Logs that contain PII must be stored in a separate bucket accessible only to the administrator. What should you do?

options.text: Upload the logs to both the shared bucket and the bucket with PII that is only accessible to the administrator. Use the Cloud Data Loss Prevention API to create a job trigger. Configure the trigger to delete any files that contain PII from the shared bucket.
On the shared bucket, configure Object Lifecycle Management to delete objects that contain PII.
On the shared bucket, configure a Cloud Storage trigger that is only triggered when PII is uploaded. Use Cloud Functions to capture the trigger and delete the files that contain PII.

Use Pub/Sub and Cloud Functions to trigger a Cloud Data Loss Prevention scan every time a file is uploaded to the administrator's bucket. If the scan does not detect PII, have the function move the objects into the shared Cloud Storage bucket.

questions.explanation:
Sensitive Data Protection can inspect Cloud Storage objects for configured sensitive-data infoTypes. Keeping uploaded logs in the administrator-only bucket, initiating an inspection through Pub/Sub and Cloud Functions, and moving only objects for which no PII is detected ensures that analysts never receive access to logs containing PII. Cloud Storage lifecycle rules and object-event triggers do not themselves evaluate an object's contents for PII.

**Learn more:** [Automating the classification of data uploaded to Cloud Storage](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sensitive-data-protection/docs/automating-classification-of-data-uploaded-to-cloud-storage) · [Inspect Google Cloud storage and databases for sensitive data](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sensitive-data-protection/docs/inspecting-storage)

questions.question: Your organization has recently experienced several DDoS attacks. You need to authenticate responses to domain-name lookups. Which Google Cloud service should you use?

options.text: Cloud DNS with DNSSEC
Cloud NAT
HTTP(S) Load Balancing
Google Cloud Armor

questions.explanation:
Cloud DNS with DNSSEC signs DNS zone data and enables validating resolvers to authenticate DNS lookup responses, helping prevent DNS spoofing and cache-poisoning attacks.\
\
**Learn more:** [DNS Security Extensions (DNSSEC) overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/dns/docs/dnssec)

questions.question: Your organization has recently experienced several DDoS attacks. You need to authenticate responses to domain-name lookups. Which Google Cloud service should you use?

options.text: 1. Enable Container Threat Detection in the Security Command Center Premium tier.2. Upgrade all clusters that are not on a supported version of GKE to the latest possible GKE version.3. View and share the results from the Security Command Center.

1. Use an open source tool in Cloud Build to scan the images.2. Upload reports to publicly accessible buckets in Cloud Storage by using gsutil.3. Share the scan report link with your security department.

1. Enable vulnerability scanning in the Artifact Registry settings.2. Use Cloud Build to build the images.3. Push the images to the Artifact Registry for automatic scanning.4. View the reports in the Artifact Registry.
1. Get a GitHub subscription.2. Build the images in Cloud Build and store them in GitHub for automatic scanning.3. Download the report from GitHub and share with the Security Team.

questions.explanation:
Artifact Analysis provides automatic vulnerability scanning for container images in Artifact Registry. After automatic scanning is enabled, new images pushed to Artifact Registry are scanned and their vulnerability results can be viewed within Google Cloud. Container Threat Detection instead monitors runtime activity in containers for attacks; it is not the image-vulnerability scanning service.

**Learn more:** [Artifact analysis and vulnerability scanning](https://cloud.google.com/artifact-registry/docs/analysis) · [Enable or disable automatic scanning](https://cloud.google.com/artifact-analysis/docs/enable-automatic-scanning)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You created an OS image hardened to your organization’s security standards and stored it in a project managed by the security team. As a Google Cloud administrator, you must ensure that every VM in your Google Cloud organization can use only that specific OS image while minimizing operational overhead. What should you do? (Choose two.)

options.text: Grant users the compute.imageUser role in their own projects.
Grant users the compute.imageUser role in the OS image project.
Store the image in every project that is spun up in your organization.
Set up an image access organization policy constraint, and list the security team managed project in the project's allow list.
Remove VM instance creation permission from users of the projects, and only allow you and your team to create VM instances.

questions.explanation:
The `roles/compute.imageUser` role in the project hosting the custom image grants principals permission to use that shared image. The `constraints/compute.trustedImageProjects` organization policy can centrally allow only the security team’s image project, restricting new VM boot disks to trusted image projects throughout the organization.

**Learn more:** [Manage access to custom images](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/images/managing-access-custom-images) · [Setting up trusted image policies](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/images/restricting-image-access)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to export and audit security logs for Google Cloud console login activity and API calls that change configurations on Google Cloud resources. The export must meet these requirements:  
  
- Export the related logs for every project in the Google Cloud organization.  
- Export logs to an external SIEM in near real time.  
  
What should you do? (Choose two.)

options.text: Create a Log Sink at the organization level with a Pub/Sub destination.
Create a Log Sink at the organization level with the includeChildren parameter, and set the destination to a Pub/Sub topic.
Enable Data Access audit logs at the organization level to apply to all projects.
Enable Google Workspace audit logs to be shared with Google Cloud in the Admin Console.
Ensure that the SIEM processes the AuthenticationInfo field in the audit log entry to gather identity information.

questions.explanation:
An organization-level aggregated log sink with `includeChildren` exports matching logs from all child projects, and a Pub/Sub topic provides a near-real-time integration point for an external SIEM. Google Workspace Login Audit logs record user sign-ins; sharing Google Workspace audit logs with Google Cloud makes those login events available in Cloud Logging. Configuration-changing API calls are recorded as Admin Activity audit logs, which are always written.

**Learn more:** [Collate and route organization- and folder-level logs to supported destinations](https://docs.cloud.google.com/logging/docs/export/aggregated_sinks) · [View and manage audit logs for Google Workspace](https://docs.cloud.google.com/logging/docs/audit/configure-gsuite-audit-logs)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to configure a Cloud Interconnect connection between your company’s on-premises data center and a VPC host network. You want to ensure that on-premises applications can access Google APIs only over Cloud Interconnect, rather than through the public internet. You must use only APIs supported by VPC Service Controls to mitigate the risk of exfiltration to unsupported APIs. How should the network be configured?

options.text: Enable Private Google Access on the regional subnets and global dynamic routing mode.
Create a CNAME to map *.googleapis.com to restricted.googleapis.com, and create A records for restricted.googleapis.com mapped to 199.36.153.8/30.
Use private.googleapis.com to access Google APIs using a set of IP addresses only routable from within Google Cloud, which are advertised as routes over the connection.
Use restricted googleapis.com to access Google APIs using a set of IP addresses only routable from within Google Cloud, which are advertised as routes over the Cloud Interconnect connection.

questions.explanation:
`restricted.googleapis.com` uses the restricted VIP, which is intended for APIs and services supported by VPC Service Controls and denies access to unsupported APIs. Advertising its VIP range to the on-premises network through Cloud Router over Cloud Interconnect lets on-premises requests reach Google APIs privately through the VPC rather than via the public internet.

**Learn more:** [Set up private connectivity to Google APIs and services](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vpc-service-controls/docs/set-up-private-connectivity?hl=en) · [Private Google Access with VPC Service Controls](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vpc-service-controls/docs/private-connectivity?hl=en)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],To make your company messaging app compliant with FIPS 140-2, a decision was made to use GCP compute and network services. The messaging app architecture includes a Managed Instance Group (MIG) that manages a cluster of Compute Engine instances. The instances use Local SSDs for data caching and UDP for instance-to-instance communication. The app development team is willing to make any changes needed to comply with the standard.  
  
Which option should you recommend to meet the requirements?

options.text: Encrypt all cache storage and VM-to-VM communication using the BoringCrypto module.
Set Disk Encryption on the Instance Template used by the MIG to customer-managed key and use BoringSSL for all data transit between instances.
Change the app instance-to-instance communications from UDP to TCP and enable BoringSSL on clients' TLS connections.
Set Disk Encryption on the Instance Template used by the MIG to Google-managed Key and use BoringSSL library on all instance-to-instance communications.

questions.explanation:
Compute Engine automatically encrypts Local SSD data, and Local SSDs do not support customer-managed encryption keys. For application traffic, using TCP enables TLS connections implemented with BoringSSL, whose BoringCrypto core is FIPS validated. Replacing UDP instance-to-instance traffic with TCP and using BoringSSL for TLS therefore addresses the required encryption in transit without attempting unsupported Local SSD key configuration.

**Learn more:** [About Local SSD disks](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/disks/local-ssd) · [FIPS 140-2 Validated - Compliance](https://cloud.google.com/security/compliance/fips-140-2-validated)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],The company recently enabled Security Command Center at the organization level. You need to implement runtime threat detection for applications running in containers in projects within the production folder. Specifically, you must be notified when additional libraries are loaded or malicious scripts are executed in these running containers. Configure Security Command Center to satisfy this requirement while ensuring that findings are visible in Security Command Center. What should you do?

options.text: Create log-based metrics and alerts in Cloud Logging and Cloud Monitoring for suspicious container activity within the production folder.
Configure Security Health Analytics within Security Command Center to monitor container runtime vulnerabilities in the production folder.
Ensure that the containers in the production folder are running on hosts that are using Container-Optimized OS.
Enable Container Threat Detection in Security Command Center Premium tier for the projects within the production folder.

questions.explanation:
Container Threat Detection monitors container runtime activity and produces Security Command Center findings for events such as added-library loading and malicious script execution. It is a Security Command Center Premium-tier capability, so enabling it for the projects in the production folder provides the required detection and makes the resulting findings available in Security Command Center.

**Learn more:** [Container Threat Detection overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/security-command-center/docs/concepts-container-threat-detection-overview) · [Use Container Threat Detection](https://docs.cloud.google.com/security-command-center/docs/how-to-use-container-threat-detection)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to establish a secure internal network in Google Cloud for database servers. The servers must have no direct access to the public internet. What should you do?

options.text: Assign a private IP address to each database server. Use a NAT gateway to provide internet connectivity to the database servers.
Assign a static public IP address to each database server. Use firewall rules to restrict external access.
Create a VPC with a private subnet. Assign a private IP address to each database server.
Assign both a private IP address and a public IP address to each database server.

questions.explanation:
A VPC private subnet with private IP addresses keeps the database servers on internal, non-internet-routable addressing. Google Cloud documents that internal IP addresses are not publicly routable and cannot be reached from the internet; external IP addresses enable communication with the public internet.

**Learn more:** [IP addresses | Virtual Private Cloud | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vpc/docs/ip-addresses) · [Subnets | Virtual Private Cloud | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vpc/docs/subnets)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An organization is beginning to move its infrastructure from its on-premises environment to Google Cloud Platform (GCP). As its initial step, the organization wants to migrate its ongoing data backup and disaster recovery solutions to GCP. Migration of the organization's on-premises production environment to GCP will be the next phase. Stable network connectivity between the on-premises environment and GCP is also being implemented.  
  
Which GCP solution should the organization use?

options.text: BigQuery using a data pipeline job with continuous updates via Cloud VPN
Cloud Storage using a scheduled task and gsutil via Cloud Interconnect
Compute Engines Virtual Machines using Persistent Disk via Cloud Interconnect
Cloud Datastore using regularly scheduled batch upload jobs via Cloud VPN

questions.explanation:
Cloud Storage is designed to hold backup files and supports scheduled transfers from an on-premises environment. Cloud Interconnect provides stable private connectivity to Google Cloud, making scheduled `gsutil` uploads to Cloud Storage an appropriate backup and disaster-recovery solution before migrating production workloads.

**Learn more:** [Disaster recovery scenarios for data](https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/dr-scenarios-for-data) · [Disaster recovery building blocks](https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/dr-scenarios-building-blocks)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization uses AI to improve products through innovation. The developers want to use Gemini in Vertex AI for a project. You must provide a secure Google Cloud environment that prevents and detects information leakages. What should you do?

options.text: Set up VPC Service Controls perimeters around the Vertex AI project. Enable Data Loss Prevention API for content inspection.
Grant the developers and AI engineers the Vertex AI User role. Monitor the audit trails with Cloud Logging.
Deploy Model Armor to protect the Vertex AI endpoint. Review Security Command Center findings to detect information leakages.
Implement a firewall rule that allows all traffic to and from the Vertex AI API endpoint.

questions.explanation:
VPC Service Controls service perimeters protect Vertex AI by restricting access across a defined boundary, which mitigates data-exfiltration risks. Sensitive Data Protection’s DLP API can inspect text content and identify sensitive-data findings, enabling detection of information that should not be exposed. [VPC Service Controls supported products](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vpc-service-controls/docs/supported-products) and [Inspecting text for sensitive data](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sensitive-data-protection/docs/inspecting-text?hl=en) describe these capabilities.

**Learn more:** [VPC Service Controls supported products and limitations](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vpc-service-controls/docs/supported-products) · [Inspecting text for sensitive data](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sensitive-data-protection/docs/inspecting-text?hl=en)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to create a VPC that lets the security team control network resources, including firewall rules. How should the network be configured to support separation of duties for network resources?

options.text: Set up multiple VPC networks, and set up multi-NIC virtual appliances to connect the networks.
Set up VPC Network Peering, and allow developers to peer their network with a Shared VPC.
Set up a VPC in a project. Assign the Compute Network Admin role to the security team, and assign the Compute Admin role to the developers.
Set up a Shared VPC where the security team manages the firewall rules, and share the network with developers via service projects.

questions.explanation:
A Shared VPC centralizes network administration in a host project while allowing developers to manage workloads in attached service projects. Security administrators can manage firewall rules in the Shared VPC network, preserving separation between network security control and application-resource administration.

**Learn more:** [Shared VPC | Virtual Private Cloud](https://cloud.google.com/vpc/docs/shared-vpc)

options.text: Enable Private Access on the VPC network in the production project.
Remove the Editor role and grant the Compute Admin IAM role to the engineers.
Set up an organization policy to only permit public IPs for the front-end Compute Engine instances.
Set up a VPC network with two subnets: one with public IPs and one without public IPs.

questions.explanation:
The `compute.vmExternalIpAccess` Organization Policy constraint restricts external IP addresses to an allowlist of specific Compute Engine instances. Configuring that policy to allow only the frontend instances prevents all other production instances from receiving public IPs, regardless of the engineers' Editor permissions.

**Learn more:** [Configure static external IP addresses | Compute Engine](https://docs.cloud.google.com/compute/docs/ip-addresses/configure-static-external-ip-address) · [Organization policies for Compute Engine](https://docs.cloud.google.com/compute/docs/access/organization-policies)

An organization has two VPC Service Controls service perimeters in Google Cloud: Perimeter-A and Perimeter-B. It needs to allow data to be copied from a Cloud Storage bucket in Perimeter-A to a different Cloud Storage bucket in Perimeter-B. The organization must minimize exfiltration risk, permit only the required connections, and adhere to the principle of least privilege. What should it do?

options.text: Configure a perimeter bridge between Perimeter-A and Perimeter-B, and specify the Cloud Storage buckets as the resources involved.
Configure a perimeter bridge between the projects hosting the Cloud Storage buckets in Perimeter-A and Perimeter-B.
Configure an egress rule for the Cloud Storage bucket in Perimeter-A and a corresponding ingress rule in Perimeter-B.
Configure a bidirectional egress/ingress rule for the Cloud Storage buckets in Perimeter-A and Perimeter-B.

questions.explanation:
Ingress and egress rules provide granular, directional control over cross-perimeter Cloud Storage access and are recommended over perimeter bridges when least privilege is required. An egress rule in Perimeter-A and a corresponding ingress rule in Perimeter-B allow the required one-way transfer while limiting access to the specified services, resources, operations, and identities. A bidirectional configuration permits unnecessary reverse access.

**Learn more:** [Ingress and egress rules | VPC Service Controls](https://cloud.google.com/vpc-service-controls/docs/ingress-egress-rules) · [Overview of VPC Service Controls](https://cloud.google.com/vpc-service-controls/docs/overview)

questions.question:
A customer deploys an application to App Engine and needs to check for Open Web Application Security Project (OWASP) vulnerabilities.  
  
Which service should be used to accomplish this?

options.text: 1. Set up one VPC with two subnets: one trusted and the other untrusted. 2. Configure a custom route for all traffic (0.0.0.0/0) pointed to the virtual appliance.
1. Set up one VPC with two subnets: one trusted and the other untrusted. 2. Configure a custom route for all RFC1918 subnets pointed to the virtual appliance.
1. Set up two VPC networks: one trusted and the other untrusted, and peer them together. 2. Configure a custom route on each network pointed to the virtual appliance.
1. Set up two VPC networks: one trusted and the other untrusted. 2. Configure a virtual appliance using multiple network interfaces, with each interface connected to one of the VPC networks.

questions.explanation:
A multi-NIC virtual appliance can attach one interface to each separate VPC network and act as the controlled path between them, where it can perform packet inspection and other security functions. Subnets within a single VPC have system-generated subnet routes, so ordinary custom routes cannot reliably force traffic between those subnets through an appliance. Direct VPC peering also creates direct connectivity rather than making the appliance the network boundary.

**Learn more:** [Multiple network interfaces](https://cloud.google.com/vpc/docs/multiple-interfaces-concepts) · [VPC routes](https://cloud.google.com/vpc/docs/routes)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],The security operations team requires access to security-related logs across every project in their organization. They have these requirements:  
  
- Follow the least-privilege model by receiving view-only access to logs.  
- Access Admin Activity logs.  
- Access Data Access logs.  
- Access Access Transparency logs.  
  
Which Identity and Access Management (IAM) role should be granted to the security operations team?

options.text: roles/logging.privateLogViewer
roles/logging.admin
roles/viewer
roles/logging.viewer

questions.explanation:
The Private Logs Viewer role provides the Logs Viewer permissions for Admin Activity logs and adds read-only access to private logs, which includes Data Access logs and Access Transparency logs. Granted at the organization level, it provides the required access across all projects without the write and configuration permissions included in Logging Admin.

**Learn more:** [Access control with IAM — Cloud Logging](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/access-control) · [Cloud Logging roles and permissions](https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/roles-permissions/logging)

questions.question: While conducting a security assessment of a customer architecture, you find that several VMs have public IP addresses. After recommending that the public IP addresses be removed, you learn that the VMs must communicate with external sites as part of the customer's normal operations. What should you recommend to reduce the need for public IP addresses on the customer's VMs?

options.text: Google Cloud Armor
Cloud NAT
Cloud Router
Cloud VPN

questions.explanation:
Cloud NAT enables VMs without external IP addresses to initiate outbound connections to internet destinations by translating their internal source addresses to shared external NAT addresses. It permits return traffic for those established connections while avoiding unsolicited inbound access to the VMs.\
\
**Learn more:** [Cloud NAT overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/nat/docs/overview) · [Public NAT](https://docs.cloud.google.com/nat/docs/public-nat?hl=en)

Which two settings must stay disabled to satisfy these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Public IP

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have observed an increased number of phishing attacks across your enterprise user accounts. You want to implement the Google 2-Step Verification (2SV) option that uses a cryptographic signature to authenticate a user and validate the login page URL. Which Google 2SV option should you use?

options.text: Titan Security Keys
Google prompt
Google Authenticator app
Cloud HSM keys

questions.explanation:
Titan Security Keys are physical FIDO security keys that provide phishing-resistant authentication. They use cryptographic proof bound to the legitimate sign-in origin, so a spoofed login URL cannot successfully obtain a valid authentication response. Google documents security keys as the most secure 2-Step Verification method and identifies Titan Security Keys as an available security-key option.

**Learn more:** [Use a security key for 2-Step Verification](https://support.google.com/accounts/answer/6103523?hl=en-Activity-Privacy-Controls) · [Make your account more secure](https://support.google.com/accounts/answer/46526?hl=en)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A security team wants to implement a defense-in-depth strategy to protect sensitive data stored in a Cloud Storage bucket. The team has these requirements:  
  
- The Cloud Storage bucket in Project A must be readable only from Project B.  
- The Cloud Storage bucket in Project A must not be accessible from outside the network.  
- Data in the Cloud Storage bucket must not be copied to an external Cloud Storage bucket.  
  
What should the security team do?

options.text: Enable domain restricted sharing in an organization policy, and enable uniform bucket-level access on the Cloud Storage bucket.
Enable VPC Service Controls, create a perimeter around Projects A and B, and include the Cloud Storage API in the Service Perimeter configuration.
Enable Private Access in both Project A and B's networks with strict firewall rules that allow communication between the networks.
Enable VPC Peering between Project A and B's networks with strict firewall rules that allow communication between the networks.

questions.explanation:
VPC Service Controls creates an enforced boundary for protected Google APIs and projects. Configuring a service perimeter containing Projects A and B and restricting the Cloud Storage API (`storage.googleapis.com`) keeps authorized access within that perimeter and blocks perimeter-crossing API requests, including copying Cloud Storage data to unauthorized resources outside the perimeter. IAM remains the mechanism for granting the intended reader permissions. [VPC Service Controls overview](https://cloud.google.com/vpc-service-controls/docs/overview) and [service perimeter configuration](https://cloud.google.com/vpc-service-controls/docs/service-perimeters) document that enforced perimeters deny boundary-crossing requests and mitigate data-exfiltration risks.

**Learn more:** [Overview of VPC Service Controls](https://cloud.google.com/vpc-service-controls/docs/overview) · [Service perimeter details and configuration](https://cloud.google.com/vpc-service-controls/docs/service-perimeters)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A service account key has been publicly exposed in multiple public code repositories. Log review shows that the keys were used to create short-lived credentials. You must immediately remove access associated with the service account.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Delete the compromised service account.
Disable the compromised service account key.
Wait until the service account credentials expire automatically.
Rotate the compromised service account key.

questions.explanation:
Deleting or disabling a service account revokes compromised short-lived credentials that represent that account. Disabling or deleting only the service account key does not revoke short-lived credentials already issued from that key; key rotation likewise does not immediately remove that existing access.

**Learn more:** [Create and delete service account keys | Identity and Access Management (IAM)](https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/keys-create-delete) · [Handle compromised Google Cloud credentials | Security](https://docs.cloud.google.com/docs/security/compromised-credentials)

You need to use Cloud External Key Manager to create an encryption key that encrypts specific BigQuery data at rest in Google Cloud. Which steps should you take first?

options.text: 1. Create or use an existing key with a unique uniform resource identifier (URI) in your Google Cloud project. 2. Grant your Google Cloud project access to a supported external key management partner system.
1. Create or use an existing key with a unique uniform resource identifier (URI) in Cloud Key Management Service (Cloud KMS). 2. In Cloud KMS, grant your Google Cloud project access to use the key.

1. Create or use an existing key with a unique uniform resource identifier (URI) in a supported external key management partner system. 2. In the external key management partner system, grant access for this key to use your Google Cloud project.
1. Create an external key with a unique uniform resource identifier (URI) in Cloud Key Management Service (Cloud KMS). 2. In Cloud KMS, grant your Google Cloud project access to use the key.

questions.explanation:
For a manually managed Cloud EKM key, the key is created or selected in a supported external key-management partner system, where it has a unique URI or key path. That partner system must grant the Google Cloud project access to use the key before Cloud KMS can create a Cloud EKM key version that references it.

**Learn more:** [Cloud External Key Manager](https://cloud.google.com/kms/docs/ekm) · [Create an external key](https://cloud.google.com/kms/docs/create-external-key)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are on an organization’s security team. The team has one GCP project containing credit-card payment-processing systems, web applications, and data-processing systems. You want to reduce the scope of systems subject to PCI audit standards.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Use multi-factor authentication for admin access to the web application.
Use only applications certified compliant with PA-DSS.
Move the cardholder data environment into a separate GCP project.
Use VPN for all connections between your office and cloud environments.

questions.explanation:
PCI DSS scope includes the cardholder data environment and any systems that are connected to it or could affect its security. Placing the cardholder data environment in a separate GCP project provides an isolation boundary from unrelated workloads, making it possible to limit the PCI assessment scope to the payment environment and any systems that remain connected to or security-impacting for it.

**Learn more:** [Limiting scope of compliance for PCI environments in Google Cloud](https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/limiting-compliance-scope-pci-environments-google-cloud) · [PCI Data Security Standard compliance](https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/pci-dss-compliance-in-gcp)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Customers report error messages when they access your organization's website. You suspect the web application firewall rules configured in Cloud Armor are overly strict. You want to gather request logs to investigate what triggered the rules and blocked the traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Modify the Application Load Balancer backend and increase the tog sample rate to a higher number.
Enable logging in the Application Load Balancer backend and set the log level to VERBOSE in the Cloud Armor policy.
Change the configuration of suspicious web application firewall rules in the Cloud Armor policy to preview mode.
Create a log sink with a filter for togs containing redirected_by_security_policy and set a BigQuery dataset as destination.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Armor request logging is part of external Application Load Balancer logging, so logging must be enabled on the protected backend service. Setting the Cloud Armor policy log level to `VERBOSE` adds the request details needed to troubleshoot which content triggered preconfigured WAF rules, while retaining logs of the enforcement outcome.

**Learn more:** [Cloud Armor request logging](https://docs.cloud.google.com/armor/docs/request-logging?hl=en) · [Cloud Armor verbose logging](https://docs.cloud.google.com/armor/docs/verbose-logging?hl=en)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],The Google Cloud organization distributes administrative capabilities to each team by providing a Google Cloud project with the Owner role (`roles/owner`). The organization has thousands of Google Cloud projects. Security Command Center Premium has identified multiple `OPEN_MYSQL_PORT` findings. You are enforcing guardrails and must prevent these common misconfigurations.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Create a hierarchical firewall policy configured at the organization to deny all connections from 0.0.0.0/0.
Create a hierarchical firewall policy configured at the organization to allow connections only from internal IP ranges.
Create a Google Cloud Armor security policy to deny traffic from 0.0.0.0/0.
Create a firewall rule for each virtual private cloud (VPC) to deny traffic from 0.0.0.0/0 with priority 0.

questions.explanation:
A hierarchical firewall policy associated with the organization applies across the organization’s projects and its higher-level rules cannot be overridden by lower-level rules. A deny rule for source range `0.0.0.0/0` centrally prevents public inbound exposure, including publicly accessible MySQL ports. An allow rule limited to internal ranges does not by itself block unmatched external traffic from being evaluated by lower-level VPC rules.

**Learn more:** [Hierarchical firewall policies](https://cloud.google.com/firewall/docs/firewall-policies) · [Hierarchical firewall policy examples](https://cloud.google.com/firewall/docs/firewall-policies-examples)

questions.domain: Securing communications and establishing boundary protection
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization is concerned by recent news headlines about vulnerabilities in production applications that have resulted in security breaches. You want to automatically scan your deployment pipeline for vulnerabilities and ensure that only scanned and verified containers can run in the environment. What should you do?

options.text: Use Kubernetes role-based access control (RBAC) as the source of truth for cluster access by granting “container.clusters.get” to limited users. Restrict deployment access by allowing these users to generate a kubeconfig file containing the configuration access to the GKE cluster.

Use gcloud artifacts docker images describe LOCATION-docker.pkg.dev/PROJECT_ID/REPOSITORY/IMAGE_ID@sha256:HASH --show-package-vulnerability in your CI/CD pipeline, and trigger a pipeline failure for critical vulnerabilities.
Enforce the use of Cloud Code for development so users receive real-time security feedback on vulnerable libraries and dependencies before they check in their code.
Enable Binary Authorization and create attestations of scans.

questions.explanation:
Binary Authorization can enforce a deployment policy requiring attestations that certify a container image completed a vulnerability scan. At deployment time, it verifies the required attestations and permits only verified images to run; images without valid required attestations can be blocked.

**Learn more:** [Attestations overview | Binary Authorization](https://cloud.google.com/binary-authorization/docs/attestations) · [Binary Authorization overview](https://cloud.google.com/binary-authorization/docs/overview)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization uses folders to represent different teams in its Google Cloud environment. To support Infrastructure as Code (IaC) practices, each team is given a dedicated service account during onboarding. You want to ensure that teams have comprehensive permissions to manage resources in their assigned folders while following the principle of least privilege. You must design permissions for these team-based service accounts in the most effective possible way. What should you do?

options.text: Grant each service account the folder administrator role on its respective folder.
Grant each service account the project creator role at the organization level and use folder-level IAM conditions to restrict project creation to specific folders.
Assign each service account the project editor role at the organization level and instruct teams to use IAM bindings at the folder level for fine-grained permissions.
Assign each service account the folder IAM administrator role on its respective folder to allow teams to create and manage additional custom roles if needed.

questions.explanation:
The Folder Admin role (`roles/resourcemanager.folderAdmin`) can be granted at an individual folder and provides the available permissions for working with that folder and its contained resource hierarchy. Assigning it separately to each team’s own folder grants broad management capability within that team’s boundary without granting organization-wide access. Folder IAM Admin is limited to administering folder IAM policies, while organization-level roles extend privileges beyond the assigned folder.

**Learn more:** [Resource Manager roles and permissions](https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/roles-permissions/resourcemanager) · [Access control for folders with IAM](https://cloud.google.com/resource-manager/docs/access-control-folders)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have been assigned to configure Security Command Center for your organization's Google Cloud environment. Your security team must receive alerts for potential cryptomining in the organization's compute environment and for common Google Cloud misconfigurations that affect security. Which Security Command Center features should you use to configure these alerts? (Choose two.)

options.text: Event Threat Detection
Container Threat Detection
Security Health Analytics
Cloud Data Loss Prevention
Google Cloud Armor

questions.explanation:
Event Threat Detection monitors logging streams and generates near-real-time threat findings, including cryptomining-related detections. Security Health Analytics scans cloud resources and generates findings for common security misconfigurations that could expose an environment to attack.

**Learn more:** [Cryptomining detection best practices](https://docs.cloud.google.com/security-command-center/docs/cryptomining-detection-best-practices) · [Overview of Security Health Analytics](https://docs.cloud.google.com/security-command-center/docs/concepts-security-health-analytics)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are a security engineer at a finance company. Your organization intends to store data on Google Cloud, but the leadership team is concerned about the security of its highly sensitive data. In particular, the company is concerned about internal Google employees being able to access the company’s data on Google Cloud.  
  
What solution should you recommend?

options.text: Use customer-managed encryption keys.
Use Google's Identity and Access Management (IAM) service to manage access controls on Google Cloud.
Enable Admin activity logs to monitor access to resources.
Enable Access Transparency logs with Access Approval requests for Google employees.

questions.explanation:
Access Approval lets the customer authorize eligible requests by Google personnel before they access customer data, and Access Transparency logs the actions that Google personnel take when accessing that data. Together, these controls provide approval-based restriction and auditable visibility for privileged Google administrative access.

**Learn more:** [Overview of Access Approval](https://docs.cloud.google.com/assured-workloads/access-approval/docs/overview) · [Overview of Access Transparency](https://docs.cloud.google.com/assured-workloads/access-transparency/docs/overview)

questions.domain: Securing communications and establishing boundary protection
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization is deploying a new Python application on Cloud Run. The application must connect to a MySQL database running on Cloud SQL in a separate project within your Google Cloud organization. You need to secure the connection between the application and the Cloud SQL instance while minimizing management overhead. What should you do?

options.text: Use a public IP address for the Cloud SQL instance. Integrate the Cloud SQL Python Connector into your application code to connect to the Cloud SQL instance.
Ensure that the Cloud SQL instance doesn’t have a public IP address. Configure Cloud Run to use Cloud SQL Auth Proxy to connect to the Cloud SQL instance.
Ensure that the Cloud SQL instance doesn't have a public IP address. Enforce SSL/TLS. Require the use of a trusted client certificate to connect to the Cloud SQL instance.
Ensure that the Cloud SQL instance doesn’t have a public IP address. Configure the application's IP address as an authorized network to connect to the Cloud SQL instance.

questions.explanation:
The Cloud SQL Python Connector uses IAM-based authorization and establishes an encrypted connection to Cloud SQL, avoiding the operational burden of managing SSL/TLS client certificates or authorized-network IP addresses. Cloud Run supports Cloud SQL connections over public IP using the Cloud SQL Auth Proxy or a Cloud SQL language connector. A private-IP-only Cloud SQL connection from Cloud Run also requires VPC egress configuration, such as Direct VPC egress or Serverless VPC Access.

**Learn more:** [Connect from Cloud Run | Cloud SQL for MySQL](https://cloud.google.com/sql/docs/mysql/connect-run) · [Connect using the Cloud SQL Auth Proxy | Cloud SQL for MySQL](https://cloud.google.com/sql/docs/mysql/connect-auth-proxy)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],For compliance purposes, an organization must ensure that in-scope PCI Kubernetes Pods run only on designated `in-scope` Nodes, and that these Nodes are restricted to running only the `in-scope` Pods (no other Pods may be scheduled on them). What should the organization do to meet this requirement?

options.text: Add a nodeSelector field to the pod configuration to only use the Nodes labeled inscope: true.
Create a node pool with the label inscope: true and a Pod Security Policy that only allows the Pods to run on Nodes with that label.
Place a taint on the Nodes with the label inscope: true and effect NoSchedule and a toleration to match in the Pod configuration.
Run all in-scope Pods in the namespace ג€in-scope-pciג€.

questions.explanation:
Applying a taint to the in-scope Nodes (labeled inscope: true) with effect NoSchedule, and configuring a matching toleration on the in-scope Pods, ensures that only Pods carrying that toleration can be scheduled onto those tainted Nodes. This satisfies the requirement that in-scope Nodes contain only in-scope Pods, since any Pod lacking the toleration is blocked from scheduling there. A nodeSelector by itself only directs eligible Pods toward matching Nodes but does not prevent other, non-tolerating Pods from also being scheduled on those same Nodes, so it fails the 'Nodes can only contain in-scope Pods' constraint. Pod Security Policies govern security context settings, not node placement exclusivity, and namespaces do not control which Nodes a Pod is scheduled to.

**Learn more:** [Taints and Tolerations | Kubernetes](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/scheduling-eviction/taint-and-toleration/) · [Assigning Pods to Nodes | Kubernetes](https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/scheduling-eviction/assign-pod-node/)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization has recently enabled the Security Command Center (SCC) standard tier. Several Cloud Storage buckets were accidentally made publicly accessible. You must investigate the incident's impact and remediate it.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: 1. Remove the Identity and Access Management (IAM) granting access to all Users from the buckets.2. Apply the organization policy storage.uniformBucketLevelAccess to prevent regressions.3. Query the data access logs to report on unauthorized access.

1. Change permissions to limit access for authorized users.2. Enforce a VPC Service Controls perimeter around all the production projects to immediately stop any unauthorized access.3. Review the administrator activity audit logs to report on any unauthorized access.

1. Change the bucket permissions to limit access.2. Query the bucket's usage logs to report on unauthorized access to the data.3. Enforce the organization policy storage.publicAccessPrevention to avoid regressions.

1. Change bucket permissions to limit access.2. Query the data access audit logs for any unauthorized access to the buckets.3. After the misconfiguration is corrected, mute the finding in the Security Command Center.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Storage usage logs can provide information about access requests to publicly accessible resources, whereas Cloud Audit Logs does not track access to public objects. After restricting the bucket permissions, enforcing the `storage.publicAccessPrevention` organization policy prevents applicable buckets from being made public through IAM policies or ACLs.

**Learn more:** [Public access prevention | Cloud Storage](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/public-access-prevention) · [Usage logs & storage logs | Cloud Storage](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/access-logs)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],The organization uses Security Command Center Premium as a central tool for detecting and alerting on security threats. It also wants alerts for suspicious outbound traffic targeting domains associated with known suspicious web services. What should you do?

options.text: Create a DNS Server Policy in Cloud DNS and turn on logs. Attach this policy to all Virtual Private Cloud networks with internet connectivity.
Forward all logs to Chronicle Security Information and Event Management. Create an alert for suspicious egress traffic to the internet.
Create a Cloud Intrusion Detection endpoint. Connect this endpoint to all Virtual Private Cloud networks with internet connectivity.
Create an egress firewall policy with Threat Intelligence as the destination. Attach this policy to all Virtual Private Cloud networks with internet connectivity.

questions.explanation:
Security Command Center Premium Event Threat Detection analyzes Cloud DNS logs to detect malware-related connections to known command-and-control or otherwise malicious domains and creates threat findings. Enabling Cloud DNS query logging through a DNS server policy attached to each internet-connected VPC supplies the necessary telemetry across those networks.

**Learn more:** [Overview of Event Threat Detection](https://docs.cloud.google.com/security-command-center/docs/concepts-event-threat-detection-overview) · [Test Event Threat Detection](https://docs.cloud.google.com/security-command-center/docs/how-to-test-event-threat-detection)

questions.question: Which Identity-Aware Proxy role must be granted to an Identity and Access Management (IAM) user so they can access HTTPS resources?

options.text: Security Reviewer
IAP-Secured Tunnel User
IAP-Secured Web App User
Service Broker Operator

questions.explanation:
The IAP-Secured Web App User role (`roles/iap.httpsResourceAccessor`) grants access to IAP-protected web applications and other HTTPS resources. Its `iap.webServiceVersions.accessViaIAP` permission authorizes web-resource access; the tunnel role instead authorizes IAP-secured VM tunneling.\
\
**Learn more:** [Manage access to IAP-secured resources](https://docs.cloud.google.com/iap/docs/managing-access)

options.text: Create a single new OU to configure enforcement of 2SV to certain users but not others.
Create configuration groups, and enable a phased migration to control the number of individuals in which to enforce 2SV.
In the Admin console, for each OU, check the checkbox to Allow users to turn on 2-Step Verification and set Enforcement to Off.
In the Admin console, for each OU, uncheck the checkbox to Allow users to turn on 2-Step Verification and set Enforcement to On.

questions.explanation:
Configuration groups let administrators apply 2SV settings to selected users independently of the existing departmental OU structure; group settings override OU settings. Enforcing 2SV in phased groups limits the number of users affected at one time and avoids the added administration of creating and moving users into a new OU.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have an application whose frontend runs in a managed instance group in subnet A, while its data layer is stored on a MySQL Compute Engine virtual machine (VM) in subnet B within the same VPC. Subnet A and subnet B each contain several other Compute Engine VMs. You want to allow only the application frontend to access the data on the application's MySQL instance through port 3306.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Configure an ingress firewall rule that allows communication from the src IP range of subnet A to the tag
Configure an ingress firewall rule that allows communication from the frontend's unique service account to the unique service account of the mysql Compute Engine VM on port 3306.
Configure a network tag
Configure a network tag

questions.explanation:
A VPC ingress firewall rule can use a source service account and a target service account, restricting TCP port 3306 traffic to VM instances using the frontend service account and to the MySQL VM using its distinct service account. This excludes the unrelated VMs in both subnets; a subnet source range or tags assigned to every VM in a subnet would not.

**Learn more:** [Use VPC firewall rules](https://docs.cloud.google.com/firewall/docs/using-firewalls)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You want to add a new access level to your existing VPC Service Controls perimeter. You must avoid breaking the existing perimeter with this change, while ensuring the fewest user disruptions and minimizing overhead. What should you do?

options.text: Create an exact replica of your existing perimeter. Add your new access level to the replica. Update the original perimeter after the access level has been vetted.
Update your perimeter with a new access level that never matches. Update the new access level to match your desired state one condition at a time to avoid being overly permissive.
Enable the dry run mode on your perimeter. Add your new access level to the perimeter configuration. Update the perimeter configuration after the access level has been vetted.
Enable the dry run mode on your perimeter. Add your new access level to the perimeter dry run configuration. Update the perimeter configuration after the access level has been vetted.

questions.explanation:
VPC Service Controls dry run mode evaluates a modified perimeter configuration without denying requests, logging only the policy violations so the impact can be validated before enforcement. Access levels do not have their own dry-run equivalent; Google Cloud’s documented approach is to create the intended access level, apply it to the perimeter’s dry run configuration, validate the results, and then enforce that dry-run configuration.

**Learn more:** [Dry run mode for service perimeters](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vpc-service-controls/docs/dry-run-mode?hl=en) · [Manage dry run configurations](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vpc-service-controls/docs/manage-dry-run-configurations)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your Google Cloud organization is divided into three folders: production, development, and networking. Networking resources for the organization are centrally managed in the networking folder. You discovered that projects in the production folder are attaching to Shared VPCs outside the networking folder, which could create a data-exfiltration risk. You must resolve the issue in the production folder without affecting the development folder. You need to use the most efficient and least disruptive approach. What should you do?

options.text: Enable the Restrict Shared VPC Host Projects organization policy on the production folder. Create a custom rule and configure the policy type to Allow. In the Custom value section, enter under:folders/networking.

Enable the Restrict Shared VPC Host Projects organization policy on the networking folder only. Create a new custom rule and configure the policy type to Allow. In the Custom value section, enter under:organizations/123456739123.

Enable the Restrict Shared VPC Host Projects organization policy at the project level for each of the production projects. Create a custom rule and configure the policy type to Allow. In the Custom value section, enter under:folders/networking.

Enable the Restrict Shared VPC Host Projects organization policy at the organization level. Create a custom rule and configure the policy type to Allow. In the Custom value section, enter under:folders/networking.

questions.explanation:
The `compute.restrictSharedVpcHostProjects` list constraint controls the Shared VPC host projects that projects at or below the policy resource can attach to. An allowlist of `under:folders/networking` applied to the production folder is inherited by its production projects, allowing only host projects within the networking folder while leaving the separate development folder unaffected. [Google Cloud: Organization policy constraints](https://cloud.google.com/organization-policy/reference/constraints)

**Learn more:** [Google Cloud Organization policy constraints](https://cloud.google.com/organization-policy/reference/constraints)
