You have been assigned to inspect IP packet data for invalid or malicious content. What should you do?

options.text: Use Packet Mirroring to mirror traffic to and from particular VM instances. Perform inspection using security software that analyzes the mirrored traffic.
Enable VPC Flow Logs for all subnets in the VPC. Perform inspection on the Flow Logs data using Cloud Logging.
Configure the Fluentd agent on each VM Instance within the VPC. Perform inspection on the log data using Cloud Logging.
Configure Google Cloud Armor access logs to perform inspection on the log data.

questions.explanation:
Packet Mirroring clones traffic from selected VM instances, including packet headers and payloads, and forwards it to a collector for examination. Security software such as IDS or deep-packet-inspection tools can analyze the mirrored traffic for malicious content; flow and access logs do not provide equivalent full packet-content visibility.

**Learn more:** [Packet Mirroring overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vpc/docs/packet-mirroring?hl=en) · [Use Packet Mirroring](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vpc/docs/using-packet-mirroring?hl=en)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization uses GitHub Actions as its continuous integration and delivery (CI/CD) platform. You must enable CI/CD pipelines to access Google Cloud resources in the most secure manner.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Create a service account key, and add it to the GitHub pipeline configuration file.
Create a service account key, and add it to the GitHub repository content.
Configure a Google Kubernetes Engine cluster that uses Workload Identity to supply credentials to GitHub.
Configure workload identity federation to use GitHub as an identity pool provider.

questions.explanation:
Workload Identity Federation configured with GitHub as a workload identity pool provider lets GitHub Actions workflows exchange GitHub OIDC tokens for short-lived Google Cloud credentials. This avoids storing or managing long-lived service account keys, which are a security risk. [Configure Workload Identity Federation with deployment pipelines](https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/workload-identity-federation-with-deployment-pipelines)

**Learn more:** [Configure Workload Identity Federation with deployment pipelines](https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/workload-identity-federation-with-deployment-pipelines) · [Workload Identity Federation](https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/workload-identity-federation)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to provision a corporate Google Cloud user account for every developer and operations staff member who requires direct access to GCP resources.  
  
Corporate policy requires that user identities remain in a third-party identity-management provider and that single sign-on be used. You discover that many users use their corporate-domain email addresses for personal Google accounts, and you must follow Google-recommended practices to convert existing unmanaged users into managed accounts.  
  
Which two actions should you take? (Choose two.)

options.text: Use Google Cloud Directory Sync to synchronize your local identity management system to Cloud Identity.
Use the Google Admin console to view which managed users are using a personal account for their recovery email.
Add users to your managed Google account and force users to change the email addresses associated with their personal accounts.
Use the Transfer Tool for Unmanaged Users (TTUU) to find users with conflicting accounts and ask them to transfer their personal Google accounts.
Send an email to all of your employees and ask those users with corporate email addresses for personal Google accounts to delete the personal accounts immediately.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Identity provides organization-managed Google Accounts for access to Google Cloud, and Google Cloud Directory Sync can synchronize users from a local directory into Cloud Identity. The Transfer Tool for Unmanaged Users identifies consumer accounts using a verified corporate domain and sends transfer invitations so account owners can consent to move their accounts into the managed Cloud Identity or Google Workspace domain.

**Learn more:** [Identities for users](https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/user-identities) · [Migrate consumer accounts](https://cloud.google.com/architecture/identity/migrating-consumer-accounts)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization needs to comply with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) on Google Cloud. You must implement data residency and operational sovereignty in the EU.  
  
What should you do? (Choose two.)

options.text: Limit the physical location of a new resource with the Organization Policy Service
Use Cloud IDS to get east-west and north-south traffic visibility in the EU to monitor intra-VPC and inter-VPC communication.
Limit Google personnel access based on predefined attributes such as their citizenship or geographic location by using Key Access Justifications.
Use identity federation to limit access to Google Cloud resources from non-EU entities.
Use VPC Flow Logs to monitor intra-VPC and inter-VPC traffic in the EU.

questions.explanation:
The Organization Policy Service resource locations constraint restricts the locations in which supported new resources can be created, supporting EU data residency. Operational sovereignty requires a personnel-access control such as an Assured Workloads EU control package that routes or restricts provider support access to EU-based personnel. Key Access Justifications instead records the reason for cryptographic key-access requests and can approve or deny those requests based on the justification; it does not restrict Google personnel by citizenship or geographic location. No listed choice correctly implements the required personnel-access control.

**Learn more:** [Restrict resource locations](https://docs.cloud.google.com/organization-policy/restrict-locations) · [Overview of Key Access Justifications](https://docs.cloud.google.com/assured-workloads/key-access-justifications/docs/overview)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization has recently moved sensitive customer data into Cloud Storage buckets. For compliance reasons, you must make sure that all vendor data access and administrative access by Google personnel is logged. What should you do?

options.text: Configure Data Access audit logs for Cloud Storage on the project hosting the Cloud Storage buckets.
Enable Access Transparency for the organization.
Configure Data Access audit logs for Cloud Storage at the organization level.
Enable Access Transparency for the project hosting the Cloud Storage buckets.

questions.explanation:
Access Transparency records actions that Google personnel take when accessing customer content, including administrative access. Cloud Audit Logs Data Access logs instead record access activity by principals in the customer's Google Cloud organization. Enabling Access Transparency for the organization provides the required scope for vendor personnel access logging.

**Learn more:** [Overview of Access Transparency](https://docs.cloud.google.com/assured-workloads/access-transparency/docs/overview) · [Enabling Access Transparency](https://docs.cloud.google.com/assured-workloads/access-transparency/docs/enable)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],During a routine security review, your team identifies a suspicious login attempt from an unknown IP address to impersonate a highly privileged but regularly used service account. You need to investigate effectively so that you can respond to this possible security incident. What should you do?

options.text: Enable Cloud Audit Logs for the resources that the service account interacts with. Review the logs for further evidence of unauthorized activity.
Review Cloud Audit Logs for activity related to the service account. Focus on the time period of the suspicious login attempt.
Run a vulnerability scan to identify potentially exploitable weaknesses in systems that use the service account.
Check Event Threat Detection in Security Command Center for any related alerts. Cross-reference your findings with Cloud Audit Logs.

questions.explanation:
Event Threat Detection in Security Command Center detects identity-based threats, including anomalous service-account impersonation. Reviewing its related findings and correlating them with Cloud Audit Logs supplies both alert context and the detailed audit evidence needed to investigate potentially unauthorized activity.

**Learn more:** [Privilege Escalation: Anomalous Impersonation of Service Account for Admin Activity](https://docs.cloud.google.com/security-command-center/docs/findings/threats/anomalous-sa-delegation-impersonation-of-sa-admin-activity) · [Cloud Audit Logs overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/logging/docs/audit)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization is migrating a complex application to Google Cloud. The application includes multiple internal components that interact with one another across several Google Cloud projects. Security is a major concern, and you must design an authorization scheme for administrators that follows the principles of least privilege and separation of duties. What should you do?

options.text: Identify the users who will migrate the application, revoke the default user roles and assign the users with purposely created custom roles.
Use multiple external identity providers (IdP) configured to use different SAML profiles and federate the IdPs for each application component.
Configure multi-factor authentication (MFA) to enforce the use of physical tokens for all users who will migrate the application.
No action needed. When a Google Cloud organization is created, the appropriate permissions are automatically assigned to all users in the domain.

questions.explanation:
Google Cloud IAM custom roles can be tailored to include only the permissions required for each administrator’s assigned responsibilities. Replacing broad default/basic role grants with purpose-built, narrowly scoped roles limits unnecessary access and supports separation of duties across projects and application components.

**Learn more:** [Choose which type of role to use](https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/choose-role-type) · [Use IAM securely](https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/using-iam-securely)

Your team wants to restrict users who hold administrative privileges at the organization level.  
  
Which two roles should the team restrict? (Choose two.)

options.text: Organization Administrator
Super Admin
GKE Cluster Admin
Compute Admin
Organization Role Viewer

questions.explanation:
The Organization Administrator role can manage IAM policies for organization, folder, and project resources. A Google Workspace or Cloud Identity Super Admin has full administrative access to the Admin console and is a key organization-control role. These broad organization-level privileges should be tightly restricted. [Google Cloud: Access control for organization resources with IAM](https://cloud.google.com/resource-manager/docs/access-control-org) [Google Workspace Admin Help: Make a user an admin](https://support.google.com/a/answer/172176)

**Learn more:** [Google Cloud: Access control for organization resources with IAM](https://cloud.google.com/resource-manager/docs/access-control-org) · [Google Workspace Admin Help: Make a user an admin](https://support.google.com/a/answer/172176)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company operates a website that will store PII on Google Cloud Platform. To comply with data-privacy regulations, this data may be stored only for a specified period and must be completely deleted after that period. Data that has not yet reached the period must not be deleted. You want to automate compliance with this regulation.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Store the data in a single Persistent Disk, and delete the disk at expiration time.
Store the data in a single BigQuery table and set the appropriate table expiration time.
Store the data in a single Cloud Storage bucket and configure the bucket's Time to Live.
Store the data in a single BigTable table and set an expiration time on the column families.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Bigtable supports age-based garbage-collection policies on column families. Setting a maximum age automatically removes cells whose timestamps are older than the retention period while retaining newer cells, allowing per-item retention enforcement. [Google Cloud Bigtable: Configure garbage collection](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigtable/docs/configuring-garbage-collection)

**Learn more:** [Configure garbage collection | Bigtable | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/bigtable/docs/configuring-garbage-collection)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have just created a new log bucket to replace the `_Default` log bucket. You want to route every log entry that is currently routed to the `_Default` log bucket to this new log bucket in the most efficient way. What should you do?

options.text: Create exclusion filters for the _Default sink to prevent it from receiving new logs. Create a user-defined sink, and select the new log bucket as the sink destination.
Disable the _Default sink. Create a user-defined sink and select the new log bucket as the sink destination.
Create a user-defined sink with inclusion filters copied from the _Default sink. Select the new log bucket as the sink destination.
Edit the _Default sink, and select the new log bucket as the sink destination.

questions.explanation:
The system-created `_Default` sink can be updated to use a different destination. Changing its destination preserves the sink’s existing filtering behavior while routing the log entries it accepts to the new log bucket, avoiding duplicate routing or separate filter recreation.

**Learn more:** [Route log entries | Cloud Logging](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/routing/overview) · [Route logs to supported destinations | Cloud Logging](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/export/configure_export_v2)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your Security team suspects that a former employee of your company used a service account key to obtain unauthorized access to Google Cloud resources at some point during the past 2 months. You need to verify the unauthorized access and identify the user activity. What should you do?

options.text: Use Security Health Analytics to determine user activity.
Use the Cloud Monitoring console to filter audit logs by user.
Use the Cloud Data Loss Prevention API to query logs in Cloud Storage.
Use the Logs Explorer to search for user activity.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Audit Logs record administrative and access activity on Google Cloud resources. Logs Explorer retrieves and filters audit-log entries over the relevant time range, allowing investigation of activity associated with the service account or other principal identity.

**Learn more:** [Cloud Audit Logs overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/logging/docs/audit?hl=en) · [View logs by using the Logs Explorer](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/view/overview)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A financial services company must process customer personally identifiable information (PII) for analytics while complying with strict privacy regulations. The data must be transformed to protect individual privacy while retaining its original format and consistency for analytical integrity. The solution must avoid complete irreversible deletion. What should you do?

options.text: Use Cloud Key Management Service (Cloud KMS) to encrypt the entire dataset with a customer-managed encryption key (CMEK).
Set up VPC Service Controls around the BigQuery project. Implement row-level encryption.
Implement a custom BigQuery user-defined function (UDF) by using JavaScript to hash all sensitive fields before they are loaded into the analytical tables.
Configure Sensitive Data Protection (SDP) to de-identify PII using format-preserving encryption (FPE).

questions.explanation:
Sensitive Data Protection format-preserving encryption (FPE) de-identifies PII by replacing it with encrypted tokens that preserve the input’s character set and length. FPE is reversible with the required cryptographic key, so it avoids irreversible deletion while maintaining format consistency and referential integrity for analytics.

**Learn more:** [Pseudonymization | Sensitive Data Protection](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sensitive-data-protection/docs/pseudonymization) · [Transformation reference | Sensitive Data Protection](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sensitive-data-protection/docs/transformations-reference)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company backs up application logs to a Cloud Storage bucket that both analysts and the administrator share. Analysts must access only logs that contain no personally identifiable information (PII). Log files that contain PII must be kept in a separate bucket accessible only to the administrator.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Use Cloud Pub/Sub and Cloud Functions to trigger a Data Loss Prevention scan every time a file is uploaded to the shared bucket. If the scan detects PII, have the function move into a Cloud Storage bucket only accessible by the administrator.

Upload the logs to both the shared bucket and the bucket only accessible by the administrator. Create a job trigger using the Cloud Data Loss Prevention API. Configure the trigger to delete any files from the shared bucket that contain PII.
On the bucket shared with both the analysts and the administrator, configure Object Lifecycle Management to delete objects that contain any PII.

On the bucket shared with both the analysts and the administrator, configure a Cloud Storage Trigger that is only triggered when PII data is uploaded. Use Cloud Functions to capture the trigger and delete such files.

questions.explanation:
Sensitive Data Protection can inspect uploaded Cloud Storage files for PII, and an event-driven Cloud Function can use the inspection result to move PII-containing logs to an administrator-only bucket. This creates separate storage and access boundaries for sensitive and non-sensitive logs. Cloud Storage lifecycle rules and event filters do not inspect object contents for PII.

**Learn more:** [Automating the classification of data uploaded to Cloud Storage](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sensitive-data-protection/docs/automating-classification-of-data-uploaded-to-cloud-storage) · [Using Sensitive Data Protection with Cloud Storage](https://docs.cloud.google.com/sensitive-data-protection/docs/dlp-gcs)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An organization is migrating a sensitive data-processing workflow from on-premises infrastructure to Google Cloud. The workflow collects, stores, and analyzes customer information that includes personally identifiable information (PII). You must design security measures to reduce the risk of data exfiltration in this new cloud environment. What should you do?

options.text: Encrypt all sensitive data in transit and at rest. Establish secure communication channels by using TLS and HTTPS protocols.

Implement a Cloud DLP solution to scan and identify sensitive information, and apply redaction or masking techniques to the PII. Integrate VPC SC with your network security controls to block potential data exfiltration attempts.
Restrict all outbound network traffic from cloud resources. Implement rigorous access controls and logging for all sensitive data and the systems that process the data.
Rely on employee expertise to prevent accidental data exfiltration incidents.

questions.explanation:
Sensitive Data Protection (formerly Cloud DLP) can discover and classify PII, then de-identify it using techniques such as redaction or masking, reducing the exposure of usable personal data. VPC Service Controls creates service perimeters and applies ingress and egress controls to protect Google Cloud resources from unauthorized access and data movement, directly mitigating accidental or intentional data exfiltration.

**Learn more:** [Overview of VPC Service Controls](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vpc-service-controls/docs/overview) · [Cloud Data Loss Prevention (now part of Sensitive Data Protection)](https://cloud.google.com/security/products/dlp)

questions.domain: Securing communications and establishing boundary protection
questions.question: You need to enable VPC Service Controls and permit changes to perimeters in existing environments without blocking access to resources. Which VPC Service Controls mode should you use?

options.text: Cloud Run
Native
Enforced
Dry run

questions.explanation:
Dry run mode logs requests that would violate a service-perimeter policy but does not deny them. It supports testing VPC Service Controls and evaluating changes to existing perimeters without preventing access to resources.\
\
**Learn more:** [Dry run mode for service perimeters | VPC Service Controls](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vpc-service-controls/docs/dry-run-mode) · [Service perimeter details and configuration | VPC Service Controls](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vpc-service-controls/docs/service-perimeters)

questions.question: You need to enable VPC Service Controls and permit changes to perimeters in existing environments without blocking access to resources. Which VPC Service Controls mode should you use?

options.text: Use the Organization Policy Service to create a compute.trustedimageProjects constraint on the organization level. List the trusted project as the whitelist in an allow operation.
Use the Organization Policy Service to create a compute.trustedimageProjects constraint on the organization level. List the trusted projects as the exceptions in a deny operation.
In Resource Manager, edit the project permissions for the trusted project. Add the organization as member with the role: Compute Image User.
In Resource Manager, edit the organization permissions. Add the project ID as member with the role: Compute Image User.

questions.explanation:
The Organization Policy constraint `constraints/compute.trustedImageProjects` restricts boot-disk source images to specified trusted projects. Configuring it at the organization level with the dedicated project in the allowed-value list permits that project and implicitly denies all other image-source projects.

**Learn more:** [Organization policy constraints — Define trusted image projects](https://cloud.google.com/organization-policy/reference/org-policy-constraints) · [Organization Policy overview — list rules](https://cloud.google.com/organization-policy/overview)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are exporting application logs to Cloud Storage and receive an error stating that log sinks do not support uniform bucket-level access policies. How should you resolve this error?

options.text: Change the access control model for the bucket
Update your sink with the correct bucket destination.
Add the roles/logging.logWriter Identity and Access Management (IAM) role to the bucket for the log sink identity.
Add the roles/logging.bucketWriter Identity and Access Management (IAM) role to the bucket for the log sink identity.

questions.explanation:
Uniform bucket-level access disables Cloud Storage ACLs and uses bucket-level IAM exclusively. When a log sink reports that it does not support this policy, the destination bucket must use the fine-grained access-control model instead. Cloud Storage documentation describes switching a bucket’s access-control model between Uniform and Fine-grained access.

**Learn more:** [Use uniform bucket-level access](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/using-uniform-bucket-level-access)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You intend to synchronize identities to Cloud Identity from a third-party identity provider (IdP). You found that some employees used their corporate email addresses to create consumer accounts for access to Google services. You must ensure the organization controls the configuration, security, and lifecycle of these consumer accounts.  
  
What should you do? (Choose two.)

options.text: Mandate that those corporate employees delete their unmanaged consumer accounts.
Reconcile accounts that exist in Cloud Identity but not in the third-party IdP.
Evict the unmanaged consumer accounts in the third-party IdP before you sync identities.
Use Google Cloud Directory Sync (GCDS) to migrate the unmanaged consumer accounts' emails as user aliases.
Use the transfer tool to invite those corporate employees to transfer their unmanaged consumer accounts to the corporate domain.

questions.explanation:
The transfer tool invites each unmanaged-account owner to consent to transferring the consumer account into a managed Cloud Identity account, which gives the organization control of the account and its associated data. In a federated environment, managed accounts that lack a corresponding third-party IdP identity must be reconciled so that they are not treated as orphaned and suspended or deleted. [Migrate consumer accounts](https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/identity/migrating-consumer-accounts), [Assess the impact of user account consolidation on federation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/identity/assessing-consolidation-impact-on-federation)

**Learn more:** [Migrate consumer accounts](https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/identity/migrating-consumer-accounts) · [Assess the impact of user account consolidation on federation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/identity/assessing-consolidation-impact-on-federation)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization is migrating business-critical applications to Google Cloud across multiple projects. You have only the necessary IAM permission at the Google Cloud organization level. You need to grant project access to support engineers from two partner organizations by using their existing identity provider (IdP) credentials. What should you do?

options.text: Create two single sign-on (SSO) profiles for the internal and partner IdPs by using SSO for Cloud Identity.
Create users manually by using the Google Cloud console. Assign the users to groups.
Create two workforce identity pools for the partner IdPs.

You work for an ecommerce company that stores sensitive customer data in multiple Google Cloud regions. The development team has created a new 3-tier application for order processing and must integrate it into the production environment.  
  
You must design the network architecture to provide strong security boundaries and isolation for the new application, enable secure remote maintenance by authorized third-party vendors, and adhere to the principle of least privilege. What should you do?

options.text: Create separate VPC networks for each tier. Use VPC peering between application tiers and other required VPCs. Provide vendors with SSH keys and root access only to the instances within the VPC for maintenance purposes.

Create a single VPC network and create different subnets for each tier. Create a new Google project specifically for the third-party vendors and grant the network admin role to the vendors. Deploy a VPN appliance and rely on the vendors’ configurations to secure third-party access.

Create separate VPC networks for each tier. Use VPC peering between application tiers and other required VPCs. Enable Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) for remote access to management resources, limiting access to authorized vendors.

Create a single VPC network and create different subnets for each tier. Create a new Google project specifically for the third-party vendors. Grant the vendors ownership of that project and the ability to modify the Shared VPC configuration.

questions.explanation:
Separate VPC networks create strong isolation between application tiers, while VPC Network Peering supplies the required private connectivity and preserves separate administration of the peered networks. Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) TCP forwarding provides authenticated, authorized remote access to management services such as SSH without exposing them directly to the internet. IAM access can be limited to specific vendor identities and resources, supporting least privilege.

**Learn more:** [Use IAP for TCP forwarding](https://docs.cloud.google.com/iap/docs/using-tcp-forwarding) · [VPC Network Peering](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vpc/docs/vpc-peering)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization depends extensively on Cloud Run for its containerized applications. You use Cloud Build to create images, Artifact Registry to store images, and Cloud Run for deployment. You must ensure that containers with vulnerabilities rated above a common vulnerability scoring system (CVSS) score of "medium" are not deployed to production. What should you do?

options.text: Implement vulnerability scanning as part of the Cloud Build process. If any medium or higher vulnerabilities are detected, manually rebuild the image with updated components.
Perform manual vulnerability checks post-build, but before Cloud Run deployment. Implement a manual security-engineer-driven remediation process.
Configure Binary Authorization on Cloud Run to enforce image signatures. Create policies to allow deployment only for images passing a defined vulnerability threshold.
Utilize a vulnerability scanner during the Cloud Build stage and set Artifact Registry permissions to block images containing vulnerabilities above

questions.explanation:
Binary Authorization provides a deploy-time policy enforcement point for Cloud Run. A policy can require trusted signed attestations showing that an image passed the organization’s vulnerability validation threshold, causing Cloud Run to reject images that do not meet that requirement. Artifact Analysis supplies vulnerability information that can be used with Binary Authorization to control deployment.

**Learn more:** [Binary Authorization overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/binary-authorization/docs/overview) · [Use Binary Authorization with Cloud Run](https://docs.cloud.google.com/run/docs/securing/binary-authorization)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You need to configure a Cloud Interconnect connection between your company’s on-premises data center and VPC host network. You want to ensure that on-premises applications can access Google APIs only through Cloud Interconnect, not through the public internet. You must use only APIs supported by VPC Service Controls to mitigate exfiltration risk to unsupported APIs. How should the network be configured?

options.text: Enable Private Google Access on the regional subnets and global dynamic routing mode.
Set up a Private Service Connect endpoint IP address with the API bundle of
Use private.googleapis.com to access Google APIs using a set of IP addresses only routable from within Google Cloud, which are advertised as routes over the connection.
Use restricted googleapis.com to access Google APIs using a set of IP addresses only routable from within Google Cloud, which are advertised as routes over the Cloud Interconnect connection.

questions.explanation:
`restricted.googleapis.com` provides private access to Google APIs through IP ranges that are routable only within Google Cloud and can be routed over a Cloud Interconnect VLAN attachment. It permits APIs supported by VPC Service Controls and blocks APIs that do not support VPC Service Controls, providing the required additional exfiltration-risk mitigation.

**Learn more:** [Configure Private Google Access for on-premises hosts](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vpc/docs/configure-private-google-access-hybrid) · [Private Google Access with VPC Service Controls](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vpc-service-controls/docs/private-connectivity?hl=en)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are building a new application that uses only Compute Engine VMs. Once per day, the application will run five distinct batch jobs. Every batch job needs its own dedicated set of permissions for Google Cloud resources outside your application. You must create a secure access model for the batch jobs that follows the least-privilege principle.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: 1. Create a general service account “g-sa” to orchestrate the batch jobs.2. Create one service account per batch job ‘b-sa-[1-5]’. Grant only the permissions required to run the individual batch jobs to the service accounts and generate service account keys for each of these service accounts.3. Store the service account keys in Secret Manager. Grant g-sa access to Secret Manager and run the batch jobs with the permissions of b-sa-[1-5].

1. Create a general service account “g-sa” to execute the batch jobs.2. Grant the permissions required to execute the batch jobs to g-sa.3. Execute the batch jobs with the permissions granted to g-sa.

1. Create a workload identity pool and configure workload identity pool providers for each batch job.2. Assign the workload identity user role to each of the identities configured in the providers.3. Create one service account per batch job “b-sa-[1-5]”, and grant only the permissions required to run the individual batch jobs to the service accounts.4. Generate credential configuration files for each of the providers. Use these files to execute the batch jobs with the permissions of b-sa-[1-5].

1. Create a general service account “g-sa” to orchestrate the batch jobs.2. Create one service account per batch job “b-sa-[1-5]”, and grant only the permissions required to run the individual batch jobs to the service accounts.3. Grant the Service Account Token Creator role to g-sa. Use g-sa to obtain short-lived access tokens for b-sa-[1-5] and to execute the batch jobs with the permissions of b-sa-[1-5].

questions.explanation:
Use a separate service account for each batch job and grant it only the permissions that job requires. The Compute Engine orchestration identity can impersonate each batch-job service account to obtain a short-lived OAuth 2.0 access token; the Service Account Token Creator role includes `iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken`. This preserves per-job least privilege and avoids long-lived, user-managed service-account keys.

**Learn more:** [Roles for service account authentication](https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/service-account-permissions) · [Service account impersonation](https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/service-account-impersonation)

questions.question: You are the project owner for a regulated workload operating in a project that you own and administer as an Identity and Access Management (IAM) admin. For an upcoming audit, you must provide access-review evidence. Which tool should you use?

options.text: Policy Troubleshooter
Policy Analyzer
IAM Recommender
Policy Simulator

questions.explanation:
Policy Analyzer identifies which principals have what access to Google Cloud resources from IAM allow policies, including roles and permissions within a selected project scope. This provides the access information needed as audit evidence for an access review.\
\
**Learn more:** [Analyze access to resources | IAM](https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/analyze-access) · [Policy Analyzer for allow policies | Policy Intelligence](https://cloud.google.com/policy-intelligence/docs/policy-analyzer-overview)

questions.question: You are the project owner for a regulated workload operating in a project that you own and administer as an Identity and Access Management (IAM) admin. For an upcoming audit, you must provide access-review evidence. Which tool should you use?

options.text: BigQuery using a data pipeline job with continuous updates
Cloud Storage using a scheduled task and gsutil
Compute Engine Virtual Machines using Persistent Disk
Cloud Datastore using regularly scheduled batch upload jobs

questions.explanation:
Cloud Storage provides scalable object storage suited to backup, archival, and disaster-recovery data, including low-cost archival storage classes. A scheduled task can run `gsutil` to transfer backup data periodically from the on-premises environment while production remains there.

**Learn more:** [Cloud Storage options](https://cloud.google.com/products/storage) · [Cloud Storage storage classes](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/storage-classes)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A global defense company is migrating top-secret classified data to BigQuery and Cloud Storage. National-security regulations require that the master encryption-key material never leave accredited on-premises cryptographic hardware. The company must retain the unilateral ability to revoke data access independently of any cloud provider. What should it do?

options.text: Use customer-managed encryption keys (CMEKs) for the BigQuery datasets and Cloud Storage buckets. Store the keys in Cloud Key Management Service (Cloud KMS).
Use customer-supplied encryption keys (CSEKs) by providing your own encryption keys with each data operation in Cloud Storage and BigQuery.
Import existing on-premises master encryption keys into Cloud Key Management Service (Cloud KMS). Use the imported keys for BigQuery and Cloud Storage encryption.
Configure Cloud External Key Manager (Cloud EKM) for the BigQuery datasets and Cloud Storage buckets. Integrate EKM with your existing on-premises hardware security modules (HSMs).

questions.explanation:
Cloud External Key Manager lets Google Cloud services use keys managed in an external key manager, such as on-premises HSMs, without sending the external key material to Google. Access can be revoked in the external key manager at any time, which prevents use of the protected data independently of the cloud provider. Cloud EKM supports CMEK integrations for BigQuery and Cloud Storage.

**Learn more:** [Cloud External Key Manager overview](https://cloud.google.com/kms/docs/ekm) · [Cloud KMS compatible services](https://cloud.google.com/kms/docs/compatible-services)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A large e-retailer is migrating its ecommerce website to Google Cloud Platform. The company needs to ensure that payment information is encrypted between customers' browsers and GCP when customers check out online.  
  
What should the company do?

options.text: Configure an SSL Certificate on an L7 Load Balancer and require encryption.
Configure an SSL Certificate on a Network TCP Load Balancer and require encryption.
Configure the firewall to allow inbound traffic on port 443, and block all other inbound traffic.
Configure the firewall to allow outbound traffic on port 443, and block all other outbound traffic.

questions.explanation:
An HTTPS Layer 7 Application Load Balancer uses an SSL/TLS certificate to encrypt traffic between the customer browser and the load balancer. Firewall rules can permit or deny traffic but do not provide encryption.

**Learn more:** [External Application Load Balancer overview](https://cloud.google.com/load-balancing/docs/https) · [SSL certificates overview](https://cloud.google.com/load-balancing/docs/ssl-certificates)

questions.domain: Securing communications and establishing boundary protection
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization runs an internet-facing application behind a load balancer. Regulators require end-to-end encryption for user login credentials. You must meet this requirement. What should you do?

options.text: Generate a symmetric key with Cloud KMS. Encrypt client-side user credentials by using the symmetric key.
Concatenate the credential with a timestamp. Submit the timestamp and hashed value of credentials to the network.
Deploy the TLS certificate at Google Cloud Global HTTPs Load Balancer, and submit the user credentials through HTTPs.
Generate an asymmetric key with Cloud KMS. Encrypt client-side user credentials using the public key.

questions.explanation:
TLS encrypts credentials in transit between the client and the load balancer. Configuring a TLS certificate on a global HTTPS load balancer and having clients submit credentials over HTTPS provides the required encrypted transport. Google Cloud documents that TLS provides privacy between a client and a server or load balancer.

**Learn more:** [SSL certificates overview | Cloud Load Balancing](https://docs.cloud.google.com/load-balancing/docs/ssl-certificates?hl=en)

questions.question: While onboarding new users to Cloud Identity, you discover that some users created consumer user accounts with the corporate domain name. How should these consumer user accounts be managed with Cloud Identity?

options.text: Use Google Cloud Directory Sync to convert the unmanaged user accounts.
Create a new managed user account for each consumer user account.
Use the transfer tool for unmanaged user accounts.
Configure single sign-on using a customer's third-party provider.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Identity’s Transfer tool for unmanaged users is designed to find unmanaged Google accounts using the organization’s domain and migrate them into managed accounts. Transferred accounts are then governed by the organization’s Cloud Identity policies.\
\
**Learn more:** [Before using the transfer tool](https://support.google.com/a/answer/7062710?hl=en-419)

questions.question: While onboarding new users to Cloud Identity, you discover that some users created consumer user accounts with the corporate domain name. How should these consumer user accounts be managed with Cloud Identity?

options.text: Create a Cloud Armor policy with a deny-rule for the known IP address range. Attach the policy to the backend of the Application Load Balancer.
Activate Identity-Aware Proxy for the backend of the Application Load Balancer. Create a firewall rule that only allows traffic from the proxy to the application.
Create a log sink with a filter containing the known IP address range. Trigger an alert that detects when the Application Load Balancer is accessed from those IPs.
Create a Cloud Firewall policy with a deny-rule for the known IP address range. Associate the firewall policy to the Virtual Private Cloud with the application backend.

questions.explanation:
Google Cloud Armor backend security policies support allow and deny rules that match a client IP address or CIDR range. Attaching such a policy to the backend service of an external Application Load Balancer blocks matching requests before they reach the application backend.

**Learn more:** [Google Cloud Armor security policy overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/armor/docs/security-policy-overview?authuser=6) · [Example security policies for Application Load Balancers](https://cloud.google.com/armor/docs/example-policies)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization needs to protect every workload running on a Compute Engine VM so that instances have not been compromised by boot-level or kernel-level malware. You also need to ensure that data in use on the VM cannot be read by the underlying host system through a hardware-based solution.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: 1. Use Google Shielded VM including secure boot, Virtual Trusted Platform Module (vTPM), and integrity monitoring.2. Create a Cloud Run function to check for the VM settings, generate metrics, and run the function regularly.
1. Activate Virtual Machine Threat Detection in Security Command Center (SCC) Premium.2. Monitor the findings in SCC.

1. Use Google Shielded VM including secure boot, Virtual Trusted Platform Module (vTPM), and integrity monitoring.2. Activate Confidential Computing.3. Enforce these actions by using organization policies.

1. Use secure hardened images from the Google Cloud Marketplace.2. When deploying the images, activate the Confidential Computing option.3. Enforce the use of the correct images and Confidential Computing by using organization policies.

questions.explanation:
Shielded VM uses Secure Boot, vTPM-enabled measured boot, and integrity monitoring to defend against bootkits, rootkits, and kernel-level compromise. Confidential VM uses hardware-based memory encryption in a trusted execution environment, with encryption keys inaccessible to the hypervisor, to protect data while it is in use. Organization policies can require these configurations across an organization.

**Learn more:** [About Shielded VMs](https://docs.cloud.google.com/compute/docs/about-shielded-vm) · [Confidential VM overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/confidential-computing/confidential-vm/docs/confidential-vm-overview)

A customer plans to deploy a large number of three-tier web applications on Compute Engine.  
  
How should the customer provide authenticated network separation among the application's different tiers?

options.text: Run each tier in its own Project, and segregate using Project labels.
Run each tier with a different Service Account (SA), and use SA-based firewall rules.
Run each tier in its own subnet, and use subnet-based firewall rules.
Run each tier with its own VM tags, and use tag-based firewall rules.

questions.explanation:
Compute Engine VPC firewall rules can use service accounts to identify source and target VM instances, enforcing tier-to-tier access based on authenticated workload identity. This provides identity-based network separation that subnet-, label-, and ordinary network-tag-based rules do not provide.

**Learn more:** [Use VPC firewall rules](https://docs.cloud.google.com/firewall/docs/using-firewalls) · [VPC firewall rules](https://docs.cloud.google.com/firewall/docs/firewalls)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You administer one of your organization’s Google Cloud projects (Project A). A VPC Service Controls (SC) perimeter blocks API-access requests to this project, including Pub/Sub. A resource that runs under a service account in another project (Project B) must collect messages from a Pub/Sub topic in your project. Project B is not part of a VPC SC perimeter. You need to grant Project B access to the Pub/Sub topic in Project A according to the principle of least privilege.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Configure an ingress policy for the perimeter in Project A, and allow access for the service account in Project B to collect messages.
Create an access level that allows a developer in Project B to subscribe to the Pub/Sub topic that is located in Project A.
Create a perimeter bridge between Project A and Project B to allow the required communication between both projects.
Remove the Pub/Sub API from the list of restricted services in the perimeter configuration for Project A.

questions.explanation:
An ingress policy permits an API client outside a service perimeter to access resources inside it when the policy’s source, identity, service operation, and resource constraints are satisfied. Restricting the rule to the specific service account from Project B and the required Pub/Sub subscriber access provides the required cross-boundary access without broadly connecting projects or removing Pub/Sub from perimeter protection. The service account also needs the corresponding Pub/Sub IAM permission on the applicable subscription/resource.

**Learn more:** [Ingress and egress rules | VPC Service Controls](https://cloud.google.com/vpc-service-controls/docs/ingress-egress-rules) · [Supported products and limitations | VPC Service Controls](https://cloud.google.com/vpc-service-controls/docs/supported-products)

questions.domain: Securing communications and establishing boundary protection
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company has deployed an artificial-intelligence model in a central project. The model contains substantial sensitive intellectual property and must remain strictly isolated from the internet. You need to expose the model endpoint only to a specified list of projects in your organization. What should you do?

options.text: Within the model project, create an internal Application Load Balancer that points to the model endpoint. Expose this load balancer with Private Service Connect to a configured list of projects.
Activate Private Google Access in both the model project and in each project that needs to connect to the model. Create a firewall policy to allow connectivity to Private Google Access addresses.
Create a central project to host Shared VPC networks that are provided to all other projects. Centrally administer all firewall rules in this project to grant access to the model.
Within the model project, create an external Application Load Balancer that points to the model endpoint. Create a Cloud Armor policy to restrict IP addresses to Google Cloud.

questions.explanation:
Private Service Connect can publish a service behind an internal load balancer for private consumption from other VPC networks. Its service attachment can use an explicit consumer accept list containing the authorized consumer projects, so the model endpoint remains non-internet-facing while access is limited to those projects.

**Learn more:** [Publish services by using Private Service Connect](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vpc/docs/configure-private-service-connect-producer) · [Manage published services](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vpc/docs/manage-private-service-connect-services)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are responsible for configuring Identity and Access Management in your organization’s Google Cloud environment. You must prevent your organization’s users from accessing Cloud Storage buckets in other Google Cloud organizations. What should you do?

options.text: Set a principal access boundary policy with the appropriate enforcement version. Bind the policy to the principals of your organization.
Configure organization restriction headers for your environment. Only include the organization ID of your organization in the list of allowed resources.
Create an IAM deny policy on the organization level that prevents access to Cloud Storage buckets outside the organization.
Enforce domain restricted sharing in your organization. Configure a managed constraint, and only include the principals in your organization.

questions.explanation:
Principal access boundary policies define the resources that affected principals are eligible to access, regardless of roles granted on external resources. A policy allowing only resources in the organization, bound to the organization’s principals, makes those principals ineligible to access Cloud Storage buckets in other organizations. The enforcement version determines which IAM permissions the boundary can block.

**Learn more:** [Principal access boundary policies](https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/principal-access-boundary-policies) · [Permissions that principal access boundary policies block](https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/pab-blocked-permissions)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are part of your company's development team. You discovered that your web application, hosted in staging on GKE, dynamically includes user data in web pages without properly validating the supplied data first. This could let an attacker execute gibberish commands and show arbitrary content in a victim user's browser in a production environment.  
  
How should you prevent and remediate this vulnerability?

options.text: Use Cloud IAP based on IP address or end-user device attributes to prevent and fix the vulnerability.
Set up an HTTPS load balancer, and then use Cloud Armor for the production environment to prevent the potential XSS attack.
Use Web Security Scanner to validate the usage of an outdated library in the code, and then use a secured version of the included library.
Use Web Security Scanner in staging to simulate an XSS injection attack, and then use a templating system that supports contextual auto-escaping.

questions.explanation:
Untrusted user-supplied data rendered into a page can create an XSS vulnerability, allowing attacker-controlled script or content to run in a victim’s browser. Web Security Scanner can simulate XSS injection, and the recommended remediation is to escape output through a templating system that provides contextual auto-escaping.

**Learn more:** [Remediating Web Security Scanner findings](https://docs.cloud.google.com/security-command-center/docs/how-to-remediate-web-security-scanner-findings?hl=en) · [Overview of Web Security Scanner](https://docs.cloud.google.com/security-command-center/docs/concepts-web-security-scanner-overview?hl=en)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A customer’s data science group wants to use Google Cloud Platform (GCP) for its analytics workloads. Company policy requires that all data be company-owned and that all user authentication go through its own Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) 2.0 Identity Provider (IdP). The Infrastructure Operations Systems Engineer was attempting to set up Cloud Identity for the customer and discovered that the customer’s domain was already in use by G Suite.  
  
How should you best advise the Systems Engineer to proceed with the least disruption?

options.text: Contact Google Support and initiate the Domain Contestation Process to use the domain name in your new Cloud Identity domain.
Register a new domain name, and use that for the new Cloud Identity domain.
Ask Google to provision the data science manager's account as a Super Administrator in the existing domain.
Ask customer's management to discover any other uses of Google managed services, and work with the existing Super Administrator.

questions.explanation:
A domain already used by Google Workspace/G Suite should be managed through its existing Google identity organization rather than by creating a separate Cloud Identity organization or a replacement domain. Coordinating with the existing Super Administrator lets the organization assess existing Google-managed services, retain centralized ownership and administration of identities and data, and configure federation with the organization’s SAML 2.0 IdP.

**Learn more:** [Google Cloud Setup guided flow](https://docs.cloud.google.com/docs/enterprise/cloud-setup) · [Decide how to onboard identities to Google Cloud](https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/landing-zones/decide-how-to-onboard-identities)

questions.question: You are implementing data protection by design in accordance with GDPR requirements. During design reviews, you are told to manage the encryption key for a solution that includes workloads for Compute Engine, Google Kubernetes Engine, Cloud Storage, BigQuery, and Pub/Sub. Which option should you select for this implementation?

options.text: Cloud External Key Manager
Customer-managed encryption keys
Customer-supplied encryption keys
Google default encryption

questions.explanation:
Customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK) let an organization control Cloud KMS keys used to encrypt data at rest. CMEK is supported across the listed services, including Compute Engine, Google Kubernetes Engine, Cloud Storage, BigQuery, and Pub/Sub, making it the appropriate common key-management approach.\
\
**Learn more:** [Cloud KMS compatible services](https://cloud.google.com/kms/docs/compatible-services)

questions.question: You are implementing data protection by design in accordance with GDPR requirements. During design reviews, you are told to manage the encryption key for a solution that includes workloads for Compute Engine, Google Kubernetes Engine, Cloud Storage, BigQuery, and Pub/Sub. Which option should you select for this implementation?

options.text: Use Cloud Key Management Service to encrypt PII shared by customers before storing it for analysis.
Use Object Lifecycle Management to make sure that all chat records containing PII are discarded and not saved for analysis.
Use the image inspection and redaction actions of the DLP API to redact PII from the images before storing them for analysis.
Use the generalization and bucketing actions of the DLP API solution to redact PII from the texts before storing them for analysis.

questions.explanation:
Sensitive Data Protection can inspect document images for sensitive text using OCR and redact detected PII through the DLP API’s image-redaction capability. The resulting images retain non-sensitive content for trend analysis while obscuring PII before the records are stored.

**Learn more:** [Redact sensitive data from images | Sensitive Data Protection](https://cloud.google.com/sensitive-data-protection/docs/redacting-sensitive-data-images)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization is adopting Google Cloud and needs to ensure that sensitive resources can be accessed only from devices on the internal, on-premises corporate network. You must configure Access Context Manager to enforce this requirement. The following considerations apply:  
  
- The internal network uses the IP ranges `10.100.0.0/16` and `192.168.0.0/16`.  
- Some employees work remotely but securely connect through a company-managed virtual private network (VPN). The VPN dynamically assigns IP addresses from the `172.16.0.0/20` pool.  
- Access must be limited to a particular Google Cloud project that is within an existing service perimeter.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Create an access level named
Create an access level titled
Create an access level titled
Create a new IAM role called

questions.explanation:
An Access Context Manager access level can use IP subnetworks to validate a request’s source address; listing multiple CIDR blocks allows a request from any listed range. Including both internal ranges and the VPN pool accommodates on-premises users and remote employees whose VPN addresses change within `172.16.0.0/20`. Associating that access level with the service perimeter that contains the sensitive project enforces the approved network context for access to perimeter-protected resources.

**Learn more:** [Access level attributes — Access Context Manager](https://cloud.google.com/access-context-manager/docs/access-level-attributes) · [Service perimeters REST resource — Access Context Manager](https://cloud.google.com/access-context-manager/docs/reference/rest/v1/accessPolicies.servicePerimeters)

You manage identities for your company’s Google Cloud organization. Employees often use your organization’s corporate domain name to create unmanaged Google accounts. You want to deploy a practical, efficient solution that prevents employees from doing this going forward. What should you do?

options.text: Create a Google Cloud identity for all users in your organization. Ensure that new users are added automatically.
Implement an automated process that scans all identities in your organization and disables any unmanaged accounts.
Register a new domain for your Google Cloud resources. Move all existing identities and resources to this domain.
Switch your corporate email system to another domain to avoid using the same domain for Google Cloud identities and corporate emails.

questions.explanation:
Proactively provision a managed Google Cloud identity for every employee, and automatically provision identities for new employees. A managed Cloud Identity or Google Workspace account with the same corporate email address prevents a consumer Google account from being created with that identity.

**Learn more:** [Best practices for federating Google Cloud with an external identity provider](https://cloud.google.com/architecture/identity/best-practices-for-federating) · [Evict consumer accounts](https://cloud.google.com/architecture/identity/evicting-consumer-accounts)

questions.domain: Securing communications and establishing boundary protection
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You manage several internal-only applications hosted across different Google Cloud projects. You are deploying a new application that needs external internet access. To preserve security, you need to distinctly separate this new application from the internal systems. The solution must provide effective security isolation for the new internet-facing application. What should you do?

options.text: Deploy the application within the same project as an internal application. Use a Shared VPC model to manage network configurations.
Place the application in the same project as an existing internal application, and adjust firewall rules to allow external traffic.
Create a VPC Service Controls perimeter, and place the new application’s project within that perimeter.
Create a new project for the application, and use VPC Network Peering to access necessary resources in the internal projects.

questions.explanation:
A dedicated project establishes a strong administrative and resource-isolation boundary for the externally facing workload. VPC Network Peering enables private connectivity between that project and selected necessary internal-project resources without placing the application in the same project as internal systems. Google Cloud projects are resource containers that help isolate and control access, and cross-project resource access requires mechanisms such as Shared VPC or VPC Network Peering.

**Learn more:** [Organize resources | Google Cloud Documentation](https://cloud.google.com/docs/get-started/organize-resources) · [About resource hierarchy | Google Cloud Documentation](https://cloud.google.com/resource-manager/docs/cloud-platform-resource-hierarchy)

questions.domain: Securing communications and establishing boundary protection
questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization operates a critical web application on Google Cloud that serves international customers. Rising malicious traffic aimed at this application has strained resources and resulted in periods of downtime. You need to design security controls to improve the application's resilience to web attacks, strengthen perimeter protection, and provide access control. What should you do?

options.text: Employ network load balancing for traffic distribution. Update Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) policies to allow only administrative access. Implement custom firewall rules on all external IP addresses.
Set up firewall rules on Compute Engine instances within the application's environment. Rely on load balancers for threat detection. Increase instance resources to cope with attack volume.
Configure firewall rules to block traffic from known malicious IP ranges. Set up Google Cloud Armor and implement Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) for granular access control.
Add firewall rules that restrict all internal IP ranges. Establish Cloud DNS security policies. Disable external IP addresses to reduce the attack surface. Create user groups for access control.

questions.explanation:
Google Cloud Armor security policies protect applications behind load balancers from DDoS and other web-based attacks. Firewall rules can block traffic from known malicious IP ranges, and Identity-Aware Proxy enforces granular, identity-based authorization to the application.

**Learn more:** [Cloud Armor overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/armor/docs/cloud-armor-overview?hl=en) · [Identity-Aware Proxy overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/iap/docs/concepts-overview)

options.text: Use Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) with Access Context Manager to restrict the location of Google Cloud resources.
Use the org policy constraint 'Google Cloud Platform – Resource Location Restriction' on your Google Cloud organization node.
Use the org policy constraint 'Restrict Resource Service Usage' on your Google Cloud organization node.
Use Identity and Access Management (IAM) custom roles to ensure that your DevOps team can only create resources in the Europe regions.

questions.explanation:
The Google Cloud Platform – Resource Location Restriction organization-policy constraint (`gcp.resourceLocations`) defines where supported location-based resources may be created. Applied at the organization node with Europe locations allowed, it enforces the geographic creation restriction for descendant resources.

**Learn more:** [Restrict resource locations](https://cloud.google.com/organization-policy/docs/restrict-locations)

Your organization has created a highly sensitive project inside a VPC Service Controls perimeter. You must ensure that only users who meet specific contextual requirements—such as using a company-managed device, being in a specified location, and having a valid user identity—can access resources within this perimeter. You want to assess the effect of this change without blocking legitimate access. What should you do?

options.text: Establish a Context-Aware Access policy that specifies the required contextual attributes, and associate the policy with the VPC Service Controls perimeter in dry run mode.
Use the VPC Service Control Violation dashboard to identify the impact of details about access denials by service perimeters.
Configure a VPC Service Controls perimeter in dry run mode, and enforce strict network segmentation using firewall rules. Use multi-factor authentication (MFA) for user verification.
Use Cloud Audit Logs to monitor user access to the project resources. Use post-incident analysis to identify unauthorized access attempts.

questions.explanation:
Access Context Manager access levels define contextual requirements for requests, including device data, network-origin attributes, and user identity, and can be applied to VPC Service Controls service perimeters. A perimeter dry-run configuration logs policy violations without denying requests, enabling validation of the proposed restrictions before enforcement.

**Learn more:** [Access Context Manager overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/access-context-manager/docs/overview) · [Dry run mode for service perimeters](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vpc-service-controls/docs/dry-run-mode)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization develops software that participates in many open-source projects and is concerned about software supply-chain threats. You need to provide build provenance to show that the software has not been tampered with.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: 1. Hire an external auditor to review and provide provenance.2. Define the scope and conditions.3. Get support from the Security department or representative.4. Publish the attestation to your public web page.

1. Review the software process.2. Generate private and public key pairs and use Pretty Good Privacy (PGP) protocols to sign the output software artifacts together with a file containing the address of your enterprise and point of contact.3. Publish the PGP signed attestation to your public web page.
1. Publish the software code on GitHub as open source.2. Establish a bug bounty program, and encourage the open source community to review, report, and fix the vulnerabilities.
1. Generate Supply Chain Levels for Software Artifacts (SLSA) level 3 assurance by using Cloud Build.2. View the build provenance in the Security insights side panel within the Google Cloud console.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Build can generate verifiable build provenance for container images that provides SLSA Level 3 assurance. Its Security insights side panel in the Google Cloud console displays build provenance metadata, enabling verification that artifacts originated from trusted sources and a trusted build system.

**Learn more:** [Generate and validate build provenance](https://docs.cloud.google.com/build/docs/securing-builds/generate-validate-build-provenance) · [View build security insights](https://docs.cloud.google.com/build/docs/view-build-security-insights)

questions.question: You need to recommend a solution for storing and retrieving sensitive configuration data from an application running on Compute Engine. Which option should you recommend?

options.text: Cloud Key Management Service
Compute Engine guest attributes
Compute Engine custom metadata
Secret Manager

questions.explanation:
Secret Manager is designed to store and manage sensitive application data, including configuration values such as database passwords and API keys. It supports versioned secrets and IAM-controlled access, and Compute Engine workloads can retrieve secret versions through the Secret Manager API.\
\
**Learn more:** [Secret Manager overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/secret-manager/docs/overview) · [Access a secret version](https://docs.cloud.google.com/secret-manager/docs/access-secret-version)

questions.question: You need to recommend a solution for storing and retrieving sensitive configuration data from an application running on Compute Engine. Which option should you recommend?

options.text: Create a filter set in Cloud Asset Inventory to identify service accounts with high privileges and IAM principals with Gmail domains.
Scan and alert vulnerabilities and misconfigurations by using Secure Health Analytics detectors in Security Command Center Premium.
Set up filters on Cloud Audit Logs to flag log entries for specific, risky API calls, and display the calls in a Cloud Log Analytics dashboard.
Alert and track emerging attacks detected in your environment by using Event Threat Detection detectors.

questions.explanation:
Security Health Analytics uses detectors in Security Command Center to scan cloud environments for vulnerabilities and common misconfigurations, producing findings that can be tracked for remediation. Its detectors are also mapped to compliance controls and security benchmarks, making it the appropriate capability for organization-wide configuration and compliance monitoring.

**Learn more:** [Overview of Security Health Analytics](https://docs.cloud.google.com/security-command-center/docs/concepts-security-health-analytics) · [Security Command Center overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/security-command-center/docs/security-command-center-overview)

You are developing an application running on a Compute Engine VM. The application must access data stored in Cloud Storage buckets in other Google Cloud projects. The needed bucket access varies. You need to grant access to these resources while following Google-recommended practices. What should you do?

options.text: Limit the VMs access to the Cloud Storage buckets by setting the relevant access scope of the VM.
Create IAM bindings for the VM’s service account and the required buckets that allow appropriate access to the data stored in the buckets.
Grant the VM's service account access to the required buckets by using domain-wide delegation.
Create a group and assign IAM bindings to the group for each bucket that the application needs to access. Assign the VM's service account to the group.

questions.explanation:
Compute Engine best practice is to use the VM's service account and control its access through IAM roles, rather than using restrictive access scopes. Cloud Storage IAM policies can be set on individual buckets, so each bucket can grant that service account only the role and permissions required, including across project boundaries.

**Learn more:** [Service accounts | Compute Engine](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/access/service-accounts) · [Identity and Access Management | Cloud Storage](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/access-control/iam)

You are deploying a web application hosted on Compute Engine. A business requirement requires application logs to be retained for 12 years, with data kept within European boundaries. You want to implement a storage solution that minimizes overhead and is cost-effective. What should you do?

options.text: Create a Cloud Storage bucket to store your logs in the EUROPE-WEST1 region. Modify your application code to ship logs directly to your bucket for increased efficiency.

Configure your Compute Engine instances to use the Google Cloud's operations suite Cloud Logging agent to send application logs to a custom log bucket in the EUROPE-WEST1 region with a custom retention of 12 years.
Use a Pub/Sub topic to forward your application logs to a Cloud Storage bucket in the EUROPE-WEST1 region.
Configure a custom retention policy of 12 years on your Google Cloud's operations suite log bucket in the EUROPE-WEST1 region.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Storage supports regional storage in `EUROPE-WEST1` and bucket retention periods of up to 100 years, so it can satisfy a 12-year retention requirement. Cloud Logging log-bucket retention is limited to 3,650 days (10 years), making it unsuitable as the sole long-term store. Writing logs directly to Cloud Storage avoids an additional Pub/Sub forwarding path.

**Learn more:** [Cloud Logging quotas and limits](https://cloud.google.com/logging/quotas) · [Cloud Storage Bucket Lock](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/bucket-lock)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your Google Cloud environment contains one organization node, one folder named “Apps,” and several projects in that folder. The organization node enforces the `constraints/iam.allowedPolicyMemberDomains` organization policy, allowing members from the `terramearth.com` organization. The “Apps” folder enforces the `constraints/iam.allowedPolicyMemberDomains` organization policy, allowing members from the `flowlogistic.com` organization. It also has the `inheritFromParent: false` property.  
  
You try to grant a project in the “Apps” folder access to the user [email protected].  
  
What is the outcome of this action, and why?

options.text: The action succeeds because members from both organizations, terramearth.com or flowlogistic.com, are allowed on projects in the “Apps” folder.
The action succeeds and the new member is successfully added to the project's Identity and Access Management (IAM) policy because all policies are inherited by underlying folders and projects.
The action fails because a constraints/iam.allowedPolicyMemberDomains organization policy must be defined on the current project to deactivate the constraint temporarily.
The action fails because a constraints/iam.allowedPolicyMemberDomains organization policy is in place and only members from the flowlogistic.com organization are allowed.

questions.explanation:
For a legacy list-constraint policy, `inheritFromParent: false` prevents the folder from inheriting the parent policy. The folder’s policy becomes the effective allowed-domain restriction for its descendant projects, so only members of `flowlogistic.com` can be granted IAM roles. Domain-restricted sharing blocks IAM grants to principals outside the allowed organization or domain.

**Learn more:** [Hierarchy evaluation | Organization Policy | Google Cloud Documentation](https://cloud.google.com/organization-policy/hierarchy-evaluation) · [Restrict identities with domain-restricted sharing | Organization Policy | Google Cloud Documentation](https://cloud.google.com/organization-policy/restrict-domains)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are migrating users to Google Cloud. Google web and Google Cloud CLI SDK sessions on endpoint devices are vulnerable to cookie replay attacks. You need to reduce the risk posed by these threats.  
  
What should you do? (Choose two.)

options.text: Configure Google session control to a shorter duration.
Set an organizational policy for OAuth 2.0 access token with a shorter duration.
Set a reauthentication policy for Google Cloud services to a shorter duration.
Configure a third-party identity provider with session management.
Enforce Security Key Authentication with 2SV.

questions.explanation:
A shorter Google Session control duration limits the lifetime of users’ Google web sessions. A shorter reauthentication policy for Google Cloud services limits Google Cloud and gcloud CLI sessions; its expiry invalidates the refresh token and requires the user to authenticate again. These separate controls reduce the period in which a stolen session cookie or CLI credential can be replayed.

**Learn more:** [Set session length for Google services](https://support.google.com/a/answer/7576830?hl=en-au) · [Best practices for mitigating compromised OAuth tokens for Google Cloud CLI](https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/bps-for-mitigating-gcloud-oauth-tokens)

You use Security Command Center (SCC) to safeguard your workloads and receive alerts about suspected security breaches at your company. You need to identify cryptocurrency mining software.  
  
Which SCC service should you use?

options.text: Virtual Machine Threat Detection
Container Threat Detection
Rapid Vulnerability Detection
Web Security Scanner

You use Security Command Center (SCC) to safeguard your workloads and receive alerts about suspected security breaches at your company. You need to identify cryptocurrency mining software.  
  
Which SCC service should you use?

options.text: The VM was created with a static external IP address that was reserved in the project before the organizational policy rule was set.
The organizational policy constraint wasn't properly enforced and is running in
A project level, the organizational policy control has been overwritten with an
The policy constraint on the folder level does not have any effect because of an

questions.explanation:
A project-level organization policy can override the inherited folder-level configuration. If that project-level policy allows external IP assignment, a VM in that project can receive an external IP despite the folder policy. Google Cloud documents that a child resource can overwrite a parent policy configuration, and that project-level external-IP policies can override organization-level policies.
