questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are working with a client concerned about retaining control of encryption keys for sensitive data. The client does not want encryption keys at rest to be stored with the same cloud service provider (CSP) that stores the data encrypted by those keys. Which Google Cloud encryption solutions should you recommend?  
  
(Choose two.)

options.text: Customer-supplied encryption keys.
Google default encryption
Secret Manager
Cloud External Key Manager
Customer-managed encryption keys

questions.explanation:
Customer-supplied encryption keys (CSEKs) are stored and supplied by the customer when needed; Google Cloud does not store them. Cloud External Key Manager (Cloud EKM) uses externally managed key material that remains in a supported external key-management system and is never stored in Google Cloud. These solutions satisfy the requirement to keep key material at rest outside the CSP hosting the encrypted data.

**Learn more:** [Cloud Key Management Service overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/kms/docs/key-management-service) · [Cloud External Key Manager](https://docs.cloud.google.com/kms/docs/ekm)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A customer dismisses an engineer and needs to ensure that the engineer’s Google account is automatically deprovisioned.  
  
What should the customer do?

options.text: Use the Cloud SDK with their directory service to remove their IAM permissions in Cloud Identity.
Use the Cloud SDK with their directory service to provision and deprovision users from Cloud Identity.
Configure Cloud Directory Sync with their directory service to provision and deprovision users from Cloud Identity.
Configure Cloud Directory Sync with their directory service to remove their IAM permissions in Cloud Identity.

questions.explanation:
Google Cloud Directory Sync can synchronize users from an external directory service to Cloud Identity and apply a configured deletion or suspension policy when a user is no longer present in the source directory. Removing IAM permissions only revokes Google Cloud resource access; it does not deprovision the managed Google account.

**Learn more:** [About Google Cloud Directory Sync](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/users/about-google-cloud-directory-sync?hl=en) · [Active Directory user account provisioning](https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/identity/federating-gcp-with-active-directory-synchronizing-user-accounts?hl=en)

You are migrating an on-premises data warehouse to BigQuery, Cloud SQL, and Cloud Storage. You need to configure security services for the data warehouse. Your company compliance policies require that the data warehouse must:  
  
- Protect data at rest with full lifecycle management for cryptographic keys.  
- Use a key-management provider separate from data management.  
- Provide visibility into every encryption-key request.  
  
Which services should be included in the data warehouse implementation? (Choose two.)

options.text: Customer-managed encryption keys
Customer-Supplied Encryption Keys
Key Access Justifications
Access Transparency and Approval
Cloud External Key Manager

questions.explanation:
Cloud External Key Manager lets supported Google Cloud services protect data at rest using key material that remains in an external key-management provider, separating key management from data management and retaining external control of the keys. Key Access Justifications provides the reason information associated with key-access requests and can be enforced by supported external key managers, giving the required visibility into those requests.

**Learn more:** [Cloud External Key Manager](https://docs.cloud.google.com/kms/docs/ekm) · [Overview of Key Access Justifications](https://docs.cloud.google.com/assured-workloads/key-access-justifications/docs/overview)

A customer must stop attackers from hijacking its domain/IP and redirecting users to a malicious website through a man-in-the-middle attack.  
  
Which solution should the customer use?

options.text: VPC Flow Logs
Cloud Armor
DNS Security Extensions
Cloud Identity-Aware Proxy

questions.explanation:
DNS Security Extensions (DNSSEC) authenticates DNS lookup responses using cryptographic signatures, preventing attackers from forging or manipulating DNS responses to redirect users to malicious destinations.\

questions.question: An organization is migrating applications to Google Cloud while retaining several mission-critical applications on-premises. It must transfer data at a bandwidth of at least 50 Gbps. What should it use to provide secure, continuous connectivity between the sites?

options.text: Dedicated Interconnect
Cloud Router
Cloud VPN
Partner Interconnect

questions.explanation:
Dedicated Interconnect provides a direct physical connection between an on-premises network and Google’s network for high-throughput, private connectivity. It supports multiple 10-Gbps circuits, with up to 80 Gbps in that configuration, so it can meet a 50-Gbps requirement.\
\
**Learn more:** [Dedicated Interconnect overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/network-connectivity/docs/interconnect/concepts/dedicated-overview)

questions.question: An organization is migrating applications to Google Cloud while retaining several mission-critical applications on-premises. It must transfer data at a bandwidth of at least 50 Gbps. What should it use to provide secure, continuous connectivity between the sites?

options.text: Deterministic encryption
Secure, key-based hashes
Format-preserving encryption
Cryptographic hashing

questions.explanation:
Deterministic encryption generates the same encrypted token for each occurrence of an identical input when the same cryptographic key is used. This preserves referential integrity, allowing the de-identified banking-app and third-party credit-score records to be joined without distributing the original sensitive values. It is also reversible with the original key when re-identification is required.

**Learn more:** [Pseudonymization | Sensitive Data Protection](https://cloud.google.com/sensitive-data-protection/docs/pseudonymization) · [De-identify and re-identify sensitive data | Sensitive Data Protection](https://cloud.google.com/sensitive-data-protection/docs/inspect-sensitive-text-de-identify)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization is implementing separation of duties in a Google Cloud project. A developer group must deploy new code but must not be permitted to modify network firewall rules. What should you do?

options.text: Assign the network administrator IAM role to all developers. Tell developers not to change firewall settings.
Use Access Context Manager to create conditions that allow only authorized administrators to change firewall rules based on attributes such as IP address or device security posture.
Create and assign two custom IAM roles. Assign the deployer role to control Compute Engine and deployment-related permissions. Assign the network administrator role to manage firewall permissions.
Grant the editor IAM role to the developer group. Explicitly negate any firewall modification permissions by using IAM deny policies.

questions.explanation:
Custom IAM roles enforce least privilege by granting developers only the Compute Engine and deployment permissions required for their work, while firewall-management permissions remain in a separate network-administrator role assigned to authorized network administrators. Google Cloud recommends using the most limited predefined or custom roles that meet access requirements and avoiding broad basic roles such as Editor in production.

**Learn more:** [Choose which type of role to use](https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/choose-role-type) · [Use IAM securely](https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/using-iam-securely)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization is developing a new SaaS application on Google Cloud. Strict compliance standards require visibility into privileged-account activity and potentially unauthorized changes and misconfigurations in the application's infrastructure. You need to monitor administrative actions, record changes to IAM roles and permissions, and trace potentially unauthorized configuration changes. What should you do?

options.text: Create log sinks to Cloud Storage for long-term retention. Set up log-based alerts in Cloud Logging based on relevant log types. Enable VPC Flow Logs for network visibility.
Deploy Cloud IDS and activate Firewall Rules Logging. Create a custom dashboard in Security Command Center to visualize potential intrusion attempts.
Detect sensitive administrative actions by using Cloud Logging with custom filters. Enable VPC Flow Logs with BigQuery exports for rapid analysis of network traffic patterns.
Enable Event Threat Detection and Security Health Analytics in Security Command Center. Set up detailed logging for IAM-related activity and relevant project resources by deploying Cloud Audit Logs.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Audit Logs records administrative activity and IAM permission changes, producing an immutable audit trail for configuration modifications. Security Command Center’s Event Threat Detection monitors logging streams to identify threats and suspicious identity-related activity, while Security Health Analytics detects security misconfigurations and vulnerabilities, including IAM-related issues. Together, these services provide the required visibility, detection, and traceability.

**Learn more:** [Cloud Audit Logs overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/logging/docs/audit?hl=en) · [Overview of Event Threat Detection](https://docs.cloud.google.com/security-command-center/docs/concepts-event-threat-detection-overview)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You administer a fleet of virtual machines (VMs) in your organization and have identified that many VMs are not being patched. You need to automate recurring patching for your VMs and view patch-management data across multiple projects.  
  
What should you do? (Choose two.)

options.text: View patch management data in VM Manager by using OS patch management.
View patch management data in Artifact Registry.
View patch management data in a Security Command Center dashboard.
Deploy patches with Security Command Genter by using Rapid Vulnerability Detection.
Deploy patches with VM Manager by using OS patch management.

questions.explanation:
VM Manager’s Patch service provides patch compliance reporting, including patch summary data for VMs across an organization or folder, and patch deployments that automate operating-system and software updates on recurring schedules. [About Patch | VM Manager](https://cloud.google.com/compute/vm-manager/docs/patch)

**Learn more:** [About Patch | VM Manager](https://cloud.google.com/compute/vm-manager/docs/patch) · [VM Manager overview](https://cloud.google.com/compute/vm-manager/docs/overview)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An organization is assessing Google Cloud Platform (GCP) for selected IT workloads. It uses a well-established directory service to manage user identities and lifecycle management. The organization must keep using this directory service as the `source of truth` directory for identities.  
  
Which solution satisfies the organization's requirements?

options.text: Google Cloud Directory Sync (GCDS)
Cloud Identity
Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML)
Pub/Sub

questions.explanation:
Google Cloud Directory Sync (GCDS) provisions and synchronizes users and groups from an existing directory into Cloud Identity or Google Workspace. Its one-way synchronization allows the existing directory to remain the authoritative source of truth for identity creation, management, and deletion.

**Learn more:** [Reference architectures — Identity](https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/identity/reference-architectures) · [Active Directory user account provisioning](https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/identity/federating-gcp-with-active-directory-synchronizing-user-accounts?hl=en)

questions.domain: Securing communications and establishing boundary protection
questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You have many private virtual machines in Google Cloud. From time to time, you need to administer the servers through Secure Socket Shell (SSH) from a remote location. You want to set up remote access to the servers in a way that optimizes security and cost efficiency.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Create a site-to-site VPN from your corporate network to Google Cloud.
Configure server instances with public IP addresses. Create a firewall rule to only allow traffic from your corporate IPs.
Create a firewall rule to allow access from the Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) IP range. Grant the role of an IAP-secured Tunnel User to the administrators.
Create a jump host instance with public IP. Manage the instances by connecting through the jump host.

questions.explanation:
Identity-Aware Proxy TCP forwarding creates an encrypted, IAM-controlled tunnel for SSH access to VM instances without external IP addresses. Allowing ingress from the IAP TCP-forwarding IP range and granting administrators the IAP-secured Tunnel User role enables this access while avoiding exposed public IPs, a jump host, or site-to-site VPN infrastructure.

**Learn more:** [Use IAP for TCP forwarding](https://cloud.google.com/iap/docs/using-tcp-forwarding)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You work for a global company. Because of compliance requirements, certain Compute Engine instances located in specific projects must reside exclusively in cloud regions within the European Union (EU). You must ensure that existing non-compliant workloads are remediated and stop future Compute Engine instances from being launched in restricted regions. What should you do?

options.text: Use a third-party configuration management tool to monitor the location of Compute Engine instances. Automatically delete or migrate non-compliant instances, including existing deployments.

Deploy a Security Command Center source to detect Compute Engine instances created outside the EU. Use a custom remediation function to automatically relocate the instances, run the function once a day.
Use organization policy constraints in Resource Manager to enforce allowed regions for Compute Engine instance creation within specific projects.

Set an organization policy that denies the creation of Compute Engine instances outside the EU. Apply the policy to the appropriate projects. Identify existing non-compliant instances and migrate the instances to compliant EU regions.

questions.explanation:
An Organization Policy using the resource-locations constraint can deny Compute Engine resource creation outside permitted EU locations when applied to the relevant projects. Resource-location policies apply to newly created resources and do not automatically remediate existing instances, so existing non-compliant workloads must be identified and migrated to compliant EU regions.

**Learn more:** [Restrict resource locations](https://docs.cloud.google.com/organization-policy/restrict-locations) · [Services that support restricting resource locations](https://docs.cloud.google.com/organization-policy/reference/restrict-locations-supported-services)

questions.question: A database administrator detects malicious activity in their Cloud SQL instance. The administrator wants to monitor API calls that read the configuration or metadata of resources. Which logs should the database administrator review?

options.text: Admin Activity
System Event
Access Transparency
Data Access

questions.explanation:
Data Access audit logs record API calls that read resource configuration or metadata, including operations associated with the `ADMIN_READ` permission type. These logs provide the required visibility into read activity for Cloud SQL resources.\
\
**Learn more:** [Cloud Audit Logs overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/logging/docs/audit) · [Enable Data Access audit logs](https://docs.cloud.google.com/logging/docs/audit/configure-data-access)

questions.question: A database administrator detects malicious activity in their Cloud SQL instance. The administrator wants to monitor API calls that read the configuration or metadata of resources. Which logs should the database administrator review?

options.text: Use Identity Platform to provision users and groups to Google Cloud.
Use Cloud Identity SAML integration to provision users and groups to Google Cloud.
Install Google Cloud Directory Sync and connect it to Active Directory and Cloud Identity.
Create Identity and Access Management (IAM) roles with permissions corresponding to each Active Directory group.
Create Identity and Access Management (IAM) groups with permissions corresponding to each Active Directory group.

questions.explanation:
Google Cloud Directory Sync synchronizes users and groups from Active Directory to Cloud Identity. Access to Google Cloud resources is controlled by granting IAM roles to the synchronized groups; the roles contain the permissions that correspond to the access required by each Active Directory group.

**Learn more:** [Active Directory user account provisioning](https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/identity/federating-gcp-with-active-directory-synchronizing-user-accounts?hl=en) · [Federate Google Cloud with Active Directory](https://docs.cloud.google.com/architecture/identity/federating-gcp-with-active-directory-introduction)

options.text: Remove all users from the Project Creator role at the organizational level.
Create an Organization Policy constraint, and apply it at the organizational level.
Grant the Project Editor role at the organizational level to a designated group of users.
Add a designated group of users to the Project Creator role at the organizational level.
Grant the billing account creator role to the designated DevOps team.

questions.explanation:
The Project Creator role includes the `resourcemanager.projects.create` permission. Removing all users from that organization-level role eliminates the broad ability to create projects, and assigning the designated DevOps group to the role grants that ability only to that group. Organization Policy governs resource configuration constraints rather than which identities receive project-creation permission.

**Learn more:** [Managing default organization roles](https://docs.cloud.google.com/resource-manager/docs/default-access-control?hl=en) · [Create projects](https://docs.cloud.google.com/resource-manager/docs/creating-managing-projects?authuser=5)

Your organization operates a hybrid cloud environment in which a data center is connected to Google Cloud through a dedicated Cloud Interconnect connection. You need to set up private access from on-premises hosts to Google APIs—specifically Cloud Storage and BigQuery—without sending traffic over the public internet. What should you do?

options.text: Configure Shared VPC to extend your Google Cloud VPC network to your on-premises environment. Use Private Google Access to access Google APIs.
Establish VPC peering between your on-premises network and your Google Cloud VPC network. Configure Cloud Firewall rules to allow traffic to Google API IP ranges.
Use Private Google Access for on-premises hosts. Configure DNS resolution to point to the private.googleapis.com domain.
Configure Cloud NAT on your on-premises network. Configure DNS records in a private DNS zone to send requests to 199.36.153.8/30 to access Google APIs.

questions.explanation:
Private Google Access for on-premises hosts lets systems connected through a Cloud Interconnect VLAN attachment reach Google APIs privately. DNS must direct the relevant Google API hostnames to `private.googleapis.com`, whose VIP addresses are privately routable through the connected VPC; this supports Google Cloud APIs such as Cloud Storage and BigQuery without public-internet exposure.

**Learn more:** [Configure Private Google Access for on-premises hosts](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vpc/docs/configure-private-google-access-hybrid)

Generate a data encryption key (DEK) locally to encrypt the data, and generate a new key encryption key (KEK) in Cloud KMS to encrypt the DEK. Store both the encrypted data and the KEK.

questions.explanation:
For application-layer envelope encryption, generate the DEK locally and use it to encrypt the data. A Cloud KMS key serves as the KEK to wrap the DEK, and the encrypted data is stored with the wrapped DEK; the KEK remains in Cloud KMS.

**Learn more:** [Envelope encryption | Cloud Key Management Service](https://docs.cloud.google.com/kms/docs/envelope-encryption)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization stores regulated data in Cloud Storage. Data in Cloud Storage buckets is encrypted with Google-managed encryption keys. To satisfy compliance requirements, you must update the existing data so that it instead uses customer-managed encryption keys. What should you do?

options.text: Create a new key ring and key in the Cloud Key Management Service. In each Cloud Storage bucket configuration, change the encryption type to customer-managed encryption key.
Identify which projects contain Cloud Storage buckets with regulated data. Apply the restrictNonCmekServices organization policy constraint to the identified projects or parent folder.

Create a new key ring and key in the Cloud Key Management Service. Identify which projects contain Cloud Storage buckets with regulated data. Perform a write action on all existing objects in the buckets.

Create a customer-managed encryption key. Change the encryption type in each Cloud Storage bucket configuration to the newly created key. Perform a write action on all existing objects in the buckets.

questions.explanation:
Setting a bucket’s default Cloud KMS key applies to objects written to that bucket, but it does not retroactively change existing objects. An existing object must be rewritten with a CMEK to change its encryption. Setting the newly created CMEK as the bucket default and writing all existing objects ensures the rewritten objects are encrypted with that CMEK.

**Learn more:** [Customer-managed encryption keys | Cloud Storage](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/encryption/customer-managed-keys) · [Use customer-managed encryption keys | Cloud Storage](https://cloud.google.com/storage/docs/encryption/using-customer-managed-keys)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Users report an outage in your public-facing application hosted on Compute Engine. You suspect a recent firewall-rule change is the cause. You need to test whether the firewall rules are operating correctly. What should you do?

options.text: Enable Firewall Rules Logging on the latest rules that were changed. Use Logs Explorer to analyze whether the rules are working correctly.
Connect to a bastion host in your VPC. Use a network traffic analyzer to determine at which point your requests are being blocked.
In a pre-production environment, disable all firewall rules individually to determine which one is blocking user traffic.
Enable VPC Flow Logs in your VPC. Use Logs Explorer to analyze whether the rules are working correctly.

questions.explanation:
VPC Firewall Rules Logging creates connection records when an enabled firewall rule allows or denies traffic. The records identify the applicable rule and can be analyzed in Logs Explorer, making logging on the recently changed rules the direct way to confirm whether they are causing the outage. VPC Flow Logs provide flow visibility but are not the primary per-rule match diagnostic.

**Learn more:** [VPC firewall rules logging overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/firewall/docs/vpc-firewall-rules-logging-overview) · [Manage VPC firewall rules logging](https://docs.cloud.google.com/firewall/docs/manage-vpc-firewall-rules-logging)

You administer a Google Cloud organization that has many projects in regions around the world. The projects are protected by the same Access Context Manager access policy. You created a new folder to contain two projects that process protected health information (PHI) for US-based customers. The two projects will be managed separately and need stronger protections. You are configuring VPC Service Controls for the new folder. You must make sure that only US-based personnel can access these projects and limit Google Cloud API access within them to BigQuery and Cloud Storage only. What should you do?

options.text: • Create a scoped access policy, add the new folder under “Select resources to include in the policy,” and assign an administrator under “Manage principals.”• For the service perimeter, specify the two new projects as “Resources to protect” in the service perimeter configuration.• Set “Restricted services” to “all services,” set “VPC accessible services” to “Selected services,” and specify only BigQuery and Cloud Storage under “Selected services.”

• Enable Identity Aware Proxy in the new projects.• Create an Access Context Manager access level with an “IP Subnetworks” attribute condition set to the US-based corporate IP range.• Enable the “Restrict Resource Service Usage” organization policy at the new folder level with an “Allow” policy type and set both “storage.googleapis.com” and “bigquery.googleapis.com” under “Custom values.”

• Edit the organization-level access policy and add the new folder under “Select resources to include in the policy.”• Specify the two new projects as “Resources to protect” in the service perimeter configuration.• Set “Restricted services” to “all services,” set “VPC accessible services” to “Selected services,” and specify only BigQuery and Cloud Storage.• Edit the existing access level to add a “Geographic locations” condition set to “US.”

• Configure a Cloud Interconnect connection or a Virtual Private Network (VPN) between the on-premises environment and the Google Cloud organization.• Configure the VPC firewall policies within the new projects to only allow connections from the on-premises IP address range.• Enable the Restrict Resource Service Usage organization policy on the new folder with an “Allow” policy type, and set both “storage.googleapis.com” and “bigquery.googleapis.com” under “Custom values.”

questions.explanation:
A scoped access policy isolates a folder or project subset from the organization-wide policy and permits delegation of its VPC Service Controls perimeter and access-level administration. A service perimeter can protect the two PHI projects, while VPC accessible services limits API access from VPC network endpoints to the explicitly selected services. Protecting all services and allowing only BigQuery and Cloud Storage provides the required stricter service boundary without changing the controls for the organization’s other projects.

**Learn more:** [Scoped policies | Access Context Manager](https://docs.cloud.google.com/access-context-manager/docs/scoped-policies) · [VPC accessible services | VPC Service Controls](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vpc-service-controls/docs/vpc-accessible-services)

Enforce the gcp.resourceLocations organization policy and add

questions.explanation:

Configuring a job with the appropriate healthcare-related infoType and running it across the Cloud Storage buckets identifies healthcare data in buckets outside the EU.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company uses Google Cloud and has network assets that are publicly exposed. You want to identify these assets and conduct a security audit on them using a software tool in the shortest possible time.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Run a platform security scanner on all instances in the organization.
Identify all external assets by using Cloud Asset Inventory, and then run a network security scanner against them.
Contact a Google approved security vendor to perform the audit.
Notify Google about the pending audit, and wait for confirmation before performing the scan.

questions.explanation:
Cloud Asset Inventory provides centralized, organization-wide asset metadata and supports security audits, including identifying publicly exposed resources. Discovering the external assets with it and scanning that focused set performs the required network audit efficiently without unnecessarily scanning all instances.

**Learn more:** [Cloud Asset Inventory overview](https://cloud.google.com/asset-inventory/docs/asset-inventory-overview)

A customer is working with another company to build an application on Compute Engine. The customer is building the application tier in their GCP Organization, while the other company is building the storage tier in a separate GCP Organization. This is a 3-tier web application. Communication between application components must not traverse the public internet in any way.  
  
Which connectivity option should be implemented?

options.text: VPC peering
Cloud VPN
Cloud Interconnect
Shared VPC

questions.explanation:
VPC Network Peering provides private, internal-IP connectivity between VPC networks in different Google Cloud organizations. Traffic between peered networks stays on Google’s internal network and does not traverse the public internet.\
\
**Learn more:** [VPC Network Peering](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vpc/docs/vpc-peering) · [Virtual Private Cloud overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vpc/docs/overview)

questions.question:
A customer is working with another company to build an application on Compute Engine. The customer is building the application tier in their GCP Organization, while the other company is building the storage tier in a separate GCP Organization. This is a 3-tier web application. Communication between application components must not traverse the public internet in any way.  
  
Which connectivity option should be implemented?

options.text: Cloud Identity-Aware Proxy
Cloud Armor
Cloud Endpoints
Cloud VPN

questions.explanation:
Identity-Aware Proxy provides a centralized authentication and authorization layer for HTTPS web applications, allowing authorized users to securely access protected applications over the public internet without using a traditional VPN. It can rely on the organization’s identity service, where two-factor authentication is enforced.

**Learn more:** [Identity-Aware Proxy overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/iap/docs/concepts-overview) · [Identity-Aware Proxy documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/iap/docs)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization has on-premises hosts that must access Google Cloud APIs. You need to enforce private connectivity for these hosts, minimize costs, and optimize operational efficiency.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Set up VPC peering between the hosts on-premises and the VPC through the internet.
Route all on-premises traffic to Google Cloud through an IPsec VPN tunnel to a VPC with Private Google Access enabled.
Enforce a security policy that mandates all applications to encrypt data with a Cloud Key Management Service (KMS) key before you send it over the network.
Route all on-premises traffic to Google Cloud through a dedicated or Partner Interconnect to a VPC with Private Google Access enabled.

questions.explanation:
Private Google Access for on-premises hosts can route Google API traffic through a Cloud VPN tunnel to a VPC, providing an alternative to accessing the APIs over the public internet. Cloud VPN uses IPsec and avoids the dedicated circuits, provider coordination, and higher fixed costs associated with Dedicated or Partner Interconnect when high bandwidth or low latency is not required.

**Learn more:** [Configure Private Google Access for on-premises hosts](https://cloud.google.com/vpc/docs/configure-private-google-access-hybrid) · [Cloud VPN overview](https://cloud.google.com/network-connectivity/docs/vpn/concepts/overview)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are responsible for managing your company’s identities in Google Cloud. Your company requires 2-Step Verification (2SV) for every user. You need to restore a user’s access, but the user has lost their 2SV second factor. You want to minimize risk. What should you do?

options.text: On the Google Admin console, select the appropriate user account, and generate a backup code to allow the user to sign in. Ask the user to update their second factor.

On the Google Admin console, temporarily disable the 2SV requirements for all users. Ask the user to log in and add their new second factor to their account. Re-enable the 2SV requirement for all users.
On the Google Admin console, select the appropriate user account, and temporarily disable 2SV for this account. Ask the user to update their second factor, and then re-enable 2SV for this account.
On the Google Admin console, use a super administrator account to reset the user account's credentials. Ask the user to update their credentials after their first login.

questions.explanation:
Google Workspace administrators can generate backup verification codes for a user who temporarily cannot access a second authentication method. This lets the affected user sign in and enroll a replacement factor while 2SV remains enforced; Google recommends this approach instead of turning off 2SV for a locked-out user.

**Learn more:** [Manage a user's security settings](https://knowledge.workspace.google.com/admin/security/manage-a-users-security-settings?hl=en)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are consulting for an organization that is considering migrating its data from a private cloud to Google Cloud. The organization’s compliance team is unfamiliar with Google Cloud and needs guidance on how its compliance requirements will be fulfilled on Google Cloud. One specific requirement is that customer data at rest must reside within particular geographic boundaries. Which option should you recommend to meet the organization’s data-residency requirements on Google Cloud?

options.text: Organization Policy Service constraints
Shielded VM instances
Access control lists
Geolocation access controls
Google Cloud Armor

questions.explanation:
Organization Policy Service can enforce the `gcp.resourceLocations` constraint to limit creation of supported location-based resources to approved regions or geographic location groups. This supplies an organization-wide guardrail for data-residency requirements; supported services and their data-location behavior must also be reviewed because the constraint is not itself a contractual data-storage commitment.

**Learn more:** [Restrict resource locations](https://docs.cloud.google.com/organization-policy/restrict-locations) · [Organization Policy overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/organization-policy/overview)

You have the following resource hierarchy. An organization policy exists at each node in the hierarchy as shown. Which load balancer types are denied in VPC A?  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783810658609-hp2jgipu.jpg)

options.text: All load balancer types are denied in accordance with the global node's policy.
INTERNAL_TCP_UDP, INTERNAL_HTTP_HTTPS is denied in accordance with the folder's policy.
EXTERNAL_TCP_PROXY, EXTERNAL_SSL_PROXY are denied in accordance with the project's policy.
EXTERNAL_TCP_PROXY, EXTERNAL_SSL_PROXY, INTERNAL_TCP_UDP, and INTERNAL_HTTP_HTTPS are denied in accordance with the folder and project's policies.

questions.explanation:
An organization policy list rule with `allValues: DENY` denies every value of the constraint for descendant resources. Because the organization-level policy denies all load balancer types, all load balancer creation types are denied in VPC A, regardless of the additional folder- and project-level deny lists.

**Learn more:** [Hierarchy evaluation for Organization Policy](https://cloud.google.com/organization-policy/docs/hierarchy-evaluation) · [Organization policy constraints](https://cloud.google.com/organization-policy/docs/org-policy-constraints)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A vulnerability patch has been released, and a DevOps team must update its currently running containers in Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE).  
  
How should the DevOps team do this?

options.text: Use Puppet or Chef to push out the patch to the running container.
Verify that auto upgrade is enabled; if so, Google will upgrade the nodes in a GKE cluster.
Update the application code or apply a patch, build a new image, and redeploy it.
Configure containers to automatically upgrade when the base image is available in Container Registry.

questions.explanation:
Container workload updates are performed by building an image that includes the application update or vulnerability patch and rolling out a deployment that references the new image. GKE supports updating a Deployment’s Pod image, which replaces Pods with instances using the updated image; node auto-upgrades do not patch the application software inside running containers.

**Learn more:** [Deploying a stateless Linux application | Google Kubernetes Engine](https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/stateless-apps) · [About container image digests | Google Kubernetes Engine](https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/about-container-images)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your team must ensure that its backend database is accessible only by the frontend application, and by no other instances on the network.  
  
How should the team design this network?

options.text: Create an ingress firewall rule to allow access only from the application to the database using firewall tags.
Create a different subnet for the frontend application and database to ensure network isolation.
Create two VPC networks, and connect the two networks using Cloud VPN gateways to ensure network isolation.
Create two VPC networks, and connect the two networks using VPC peering to ensure network isolation.

questions.explanation:
A VPC ingress firewall rule can restrict database-bound traffic to instances with a database target tag and permit only instances with the frontend application’s source tag. VPC firewall rules are enforced per instance, whereas placing workloads in separate subnets does not itself block traffic between them. VPC peering and Cloud VPN provide network connectivity rather than the required workload-specific access control.

**Learn more:** [Use VPC firewall rules](https://docs.cloud.google.com/firewall/docs/using-firewalls) · [Add network tags](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vpc/docs/add-remove-network-tags)

questions.question: Which load-balancer type should be used to preserve the client IP address by default while using the Standard Network Tier?

options.text: SSL Proxy
TCP Proxy
Internal TCP/UDP
TCP/UDP Network

questions.explanation:
An external passthrough TCP/UDP Network Load Balancer preserves client source IP addresses and supports both Premium and Standard Network Service Tiers. Proxy load balancers do not preserve the original client IP by default, and internal passthrough load balancers are Premium Tier only.\
\
**Learn more:** [Choose a load balancer](https://cloud.google.com/load-balancing/docs/choosing-load-balancer) · [Passthrough Network Load Balancer overview](https://cloud.google.com/load-balancing/docs/passthrough-network-load-balancer)

options.text: 1. Export logs to a Cloud Pub/Sub topic with folders/NONPROD parent and includeChildren property set to True in a dedicated SIEM project. 2. Subscribe SIEM to the topic.
1. Create a Cloud Storage sink with billingAccounts/ABC-BILLING parent and includeChildren property set to False in a dedicated SIEM project. 2. Process Cloud Storage objects in SIEM.
1. Export logs in each dev project to a Cloud Pub/Sub topic in a dedicated SIEM project. 2. Subscribe SIEM to the topic.
1. Create a Cloud Storage sink with a publicly shared Cloud Storage bucket in each project. 2. Process Cloud Storage objects in SIEM.

questions.explanation:
A project-level log sink in each development project can route logs to a shared Cloud Pub/Sub topic in the dedicated SIEM project, giving the SIEM a single feed for exactly those projects. A folder-level aggregated sink at NONPROD would also include its test and pre-production child projects, while a billing-account scope would encompass projects sharing the billing account outside the development set. Cloud Logging supports routing logs to Pub/Sub topics, and folder or organization aggregated sinks with `includeChildren` collect logs from all child resources.

**Learn more:** [Collate and route organization- and folder-level logs to supported destinations](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/export/aggregated_sinks) · [Route logs to supported destinations](https://cloud.google.com/logging/docs/export/configure_export_v2)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization works in a highly regulated industry and must enforce strict controls over temporary access to sensitive Google Cloud resources. You have used Access Approval to manage this access, but the compliance team now requires a custom signing key. They also require that the key reside in a hardware security module (HSM) outside Google Cloud. You need to configure Access Approval to use a custom signing key that satisfies these compliance requirements. What should you do?

options.text: Create a new asymmetric signing key in Cloud Key Management System (Cloud KMS) using a supported algorithm and grant the Access Approval service account the IAM signerVerifier role on the key.
Export your existing Access Approval signing key as a PEM file. Upload the file to your external HSM and reconfigure Access Approval to use the key from the HSM.
Create a signing key in your external HSM. Integrate the HSM with Cloud External Key Manager (Cloud EKM) and make the key available within your project. Configure Access Approval to use this key.
Create a new asymmetric signing key in Cloud KMS and configure the key with a rotation period of 30 days. Add the corresponding public key to your external HSM.

questions.explanation:
Access Approval can use an externally managed custom signing key through Cloud External Key Manager (Cloud EKM). Cloud EKM connects Google Cloud to a supported external key manager, allowing a signing key that remains in an external HSM to be used for signing Access Approval requests.

**Learn more:** [Overview of Access Approval](https://docs.cloud.google.com/assured-workloads/access-approval/docs/overview) · [Cloud External Key Manager overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/kms/docs/ekm)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization’s application is integrating with a partner application that needs read access to customer data in order to process customer orders. The customer data is stored in one of your Cloud Storage buckets. You have assessed the available options and determined that this activity requires service account keys. You must advise the partner how to minimize the risk that a compromised service account key causes data loss. What should you recommend that the partner do?

options.text: Scan the Cloud Storage bucket with Sensitive Data Protection when new data is added, and automatically mask all customer data.

Define a VPC Service Controls perimeter, and restrict the Cloud Storage API. Add an ingress rule to the perimeter to allow access to the Cloud Storage API for the service account from outside of the perimeter.
Ensure that all data for the application that is accessed through the relevant service accounts is encrypted at rest by using customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK).

Implement a secret management service. Configure the service to frequently rotate the service account key. Configure proper access control to the key, and restrict who can create service account keys.

questions.explanation:
Service account keys are bearer credentials: anyone holding a valid private key can authenticate as the service account and exercise its granted permissions. Frequent key rotation limits the usable lifetime of a leaked key, while secure key handling, least-privilege access control, and restrictions on key creation reduce exposure and the number of valid keys in circulation. Google Cloud recommends routinely rotating managed service account keys and limiting service account key creation.

**Learn more:** [Best practices for managing service account keys](https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/best-practices-for-managing-service-account-keys?hl=en) · [Service account key rotation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/key-rotation)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are collaborating with developers to secure custom training jobs that run on Vertex AI. For compliance purposes, every supported data type must be encrypted with key material located in the Europe region and controlled by your organization. Encryption must not affect the Vertex AI training operation. What should you do?

options.text: Encrypt the code, training data, and metadata with Google default encryption. Use customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK) for the trained models exported to Cloud Storage buckets.
Encrypt the code, training data, metadata, and exported trained models with customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK).
Encrypt the code, training data, and exported trained models with customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK).
Encrypt the code, training data, and metadata with Google default encryption. Implement an organization policy that enforces a constraint to restrict the Cloud KMS location to the Europe region.

questions.explanation:
Customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK) protect the custom-job code copy, data loaded by that code, and temporary data written to the job VM disks. CMEK does not encrypt operation metadata, which is always protected with Google default encryption. Cloud Storage model exports require CMEK configuration on the applicable bucket or objects. The CMEK key must be located in the same region as the protected compute resource.

**Learn more:** [Customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK)](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/general/cmek) · [Vertex AI EncryptionSpec reference](https://docs.cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/reference/rest/v1beta1/EncryptionSpec)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are moving an application to the cloud. The application must read data from a Cloud Storage bucket. Because of local regulatory requirements, you must keep the encryption key material entirely under your control and require a valid justification to access that key material.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Encrypt the data in the Cloud Storage bucket by using Customer Managed Encryption Keys. Configure an IAM deny policy for unauthorized groups.

Generate a key in your on-premises environment to encrypt the data before you upload the data to the Cloud Storage bucket. Upload the key to the Cloud Key Management Service (KMS). Activate Key Access Justifications (KAJ) and have the external key system reject unauthorized accesses.
Encrypt the data in the Cloud Storage bucket by using Customer Managed Encryption Keys backed by a Cloud Hardware Security Module (HSM). Enable data access logs.

Generate a key in your on-premises environment and store it in a Hardware Security Module (HSM) that is managed on-premises. Use this key as an external key in the Cloud Key Management Service (KMS). Activate Key Access Justifications (KAJ) and set the external key system to reject unauthorized accesses.

questions.explanation:
Cloud External Key Manager allows encryption key material to remain in an external system, such as an on-premises HSM, rather than being stored in Google Cloud. With Key Access Justifications, requests include a reason code that the external key system can enforce by permitting only authorized justifications and rejecting all others.

**Learn more:** [Cloud External Key Manager](https://docs.cloud.google.com/kms/docs/ekm) · [Overview of Key Access Justifications](https://docs.cloud.google.com/assured-workloads/key-access-justifications/docs/overview)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A customer’s internal security team must manage its own encryption keys to encrypt data in Cloud Storage and has chosen customer-supplied encryption keys (CSEK).  
  
How should the team perform this task?

options.text: Upload the encryption key to a Cloud Storage bucket, and then upload the object to the same bucket.
Use the gsutil command line tool to upload the object to Cloud Storage, and specify the location of the encryption key.
Generate an encryption key in the Google Cloud Platform Console, and upload an object to Cloud Storage using the specified key.
Encrypt the object, then use the gsutil command line tool or the Google Cloud Platform Console to upload the object to Cloud Storage.

questions.explanation:
Customer-supplied encryption keys are provided with each Cloud Storage operation so Cloud Storage can encrypt the uploaded object without retaining or managing the raw key. A command-line upload tool can be configured to supply the CSEK; the Google Cloud Console does not support uploading objects with CSEK.

**Learn more:** [Use customer-supplied encryption keys](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/encryption/using-customer-supplied-keys) · [Customer-supplied encryption keys](https://docs.cloud.google.com/storage/docs/encryption/customer-supplied-keys)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You manage a group of Google Cloud projects contained in a folder named Data Warehouse. A new data analysis team has been approved to perform data analysis on all BigQuery data in the projects within the Data Warehouse folder. The team must be able only to read the data and must not have permission to modify or delete it. You want to minimize the operational overhead of provisioning access while following the principle of least privilege. What should you do?

options.text: Grant the BigQuery Data Viewer role at the project level for each project within the Data Warehouse folder.
Grant the BigQuery Data Viewer role at the Data Warehouse folder.
Grant the BigQuery Data Viewer role at the dataset level for each BigQuery dataset within each project in the Data Warehouse folder.
Grant the BigQuery Metadata Viewer role at the Data Warehouse folder.

questions.explanation:
The BigQuery Data Viewer role (`roles/bigquery.dataViewer`) permits viewing and querying BigQuery data but does not provide permissions to modify or delete that data. Granting it at the Data Warehouse folder applies the role through the resource hierarchy to the BigQuery resources in its descendant projects, providing the required read access with one least-privilege binding. The BigQuery Metadata Viewer role permits metadata access only, not data access.

**Learn more:** [BigQuery IAM roles and permissions](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/access-control) · [Introduction to security and access controls in BigQuery](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/access-control-intro)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your company’s users access data in a BigQuery table. You need to ensure that they can access the data only during working hours.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Assign a BigQuery Data Viewer role along with an IAM condition that limits the access to specified working hours.
Run a gsutil script that assigns a BigQuery Data Viewer role, and remove it only during the specified working hours.
Assign a BigQuery Data Viewer role to a service account that adds and removes the users daily during the specified working hours.
Configure Cloud Scheduler so that it triggers a Cloud Functions instance that modifies the organizational policy constraint for BigQuery during the specified working hours.

questions.explanation:
BigQuery IAM Conditions can restrict a role binding using `request.time`, including access that recurs during specified hours of the day. Applying a time-based IAM condition to the BigQuery Data Viewer role allows users to read the data only within the defined working-hours window.

**Learn more:** [Control access with IAM Conditions | BigQuery](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/conditions) · [Attribute reference for IAM Conditions](https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/conditions-attribute-reference)

options.text: Configure the GKE nodes to use the default Compute Engine service account.

Enable Workload Identity for GKE. Assign a Kubernetes service account to the application and configure that Kubernetes service account to act as an Identity and Access Management (IAM) service account. Grant the required roles to the IAM service account.
Create a user-managed service account with only the roles required for the specific workload. Assign this service account to the GKE nodes.

Create an application-specific IAM service account and generate a user-managed service account key for it. Inject the key to the workload by storing it as a Kubernetes secret within the same namespace as the application.

questions.explanation:
Workload Identity Federation for GKE is the recommended authentication method for GKE workloads accessing Google Cloud services. It provides a distinct, fine-grained identity for the application and permits least-privilege IAM role assignment without sharing the node service account or distributing long-lived service account keys in Kubernetes Secrets.

**Learn more:** [About Workload Identity Federation for GKE](https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/workload-identity) · [Authenticate to Google Cloud APIs from GKE workloads](https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/workload-identity)

You are building a new infrastructure CI/CD pipeline to deploy hundreds of ephemeral projects in your Google Cloud organization so that users can interact with Google Cloud. You want to limit use of the default networks across your organization while following Google-recommended best practices. What should you do?

options.text: Enable the constraints/compute.skipDefaultNetworkCreation organization policy constraint at the organization level.
Create a cron job to trigger a daily Cloud Function to automatically delete all default networks for each project.
Grant your users the IAM Owner role at the organization level. Create a VPC Service Controls perimeter around the project that restricts the compute.googleapis.com API.
Only allow your users to use your CI/CD pipeline with a predefined set of infrastructure templates they can deploy to skip the creation of the default networks.

questions.explanation:
The `constraints/compute.skipDefaultNetworkCreation` Boolean organization policy prevents automatic creation of the default VPC network and its related resources during project creation. Enforcing it at the organization level applies the control consistently to descendant projects, including ephemeral projects created by the CI/CD pipeline.

**Learn more:** [Organization policies for Compute Engine](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/access/organization-policies) · [Secure enterprise foundation controls](https://cloud.google.com/docs/security/security-best-practices-catalog/secure-enterprise-foundations)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Your organization uses the top-level folder to separate application environments (prod and dev). Developers must be able to view all application development audit logs, but they must not review production logs. Your security team must be able to review all logs in both production and development environments. You need to grant Identity and Access Management (IAM) roles at the appropriate resource level for the developers and security team while ensuring least privilege.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: 1. Grant logging.viewer role to the security team at the organization resource level.2. Grant logging.viewer role to the developer team at the folder resource level that contains all the dev projects.
1. Grant logging.viewer role to the security team at the organization resource level.2. Grant logging.admin role to the developer team at the organization resource level.
1. Grant logging.admin role to the security team at the organization resource level.2. Grant logging.viewer role to the developer team at the folder resource level that contains all the dev projects.
1. Grant logging.admin role to the security team at the organization resource level.2. Grant logging.admin role to the developer team at the organization resource level.

questions.explanation:
The Logs Viewer role provides read access to logs. Granting it at the organization level lets the security team view logs throughout both environments. Granting the same role on the folder containing all development projects lets developers view logs inherited by those projects while excluding production. Logging Admin includes broader log-management permissions and is not required for viewing logs.

**Learn more:** [Cloud Logging roles and permissions](https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/roles-permissions/logging) · [IAM roles for auditing-related job functions](https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/job-functions/auditing)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A financial-modeling application is already deployed on Google Cloud and processes large volumes of sensitive customer financial data. Its code is old and not well understood by the current software engineers. Recent threat-modeling exercises identified a potential risk of sophisticated side-channel attacks against the application while it runs.  
  
You need to further harden the Google Cloud solution to mitigate this side-channel-attack risk, provide maximum protection for the confidentiality of financial data during processing, and minimize application issues. What should you do?

options.text: Enforce stricter access controls for Compute Engine instances by using service accounts, least privilege IAM policies, and limit network access.
Implement a runtime library designed to introduce noise and timing variations into the application's execution which will disrupt side-channel attack.
Migrate the application to Confidential VMs to provide hardware-level encryption of memory and protect sensitive data during processing.
Utilize customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK) to ensure complete control over the encryption process.

questions.explanation:
Confidential VMs use a hardware-based trusted execution environment and memory encryption to protect code and sensitive data while they are in use. This protects confidentiality during processing without requiring modifications to the legacy application, making it the appropriate control for this requirement. [Google Cloud Confidential VM overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/confidential-computing/confidential-vm/docs/confidential-vm-overview?hl=en)

**Learn more:** [Confidential VM overview | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/confidential-computing/confidential-vm/docs/confidential-vm-overview?hl=en) · [About Confidential VM | Compute Engine | Google Cloud Documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/compute/docs/about-confidential-vm)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are developing your company’s incident-response plan. Define the access approach your DevOps team will use to review and investigate a deployment issue in your Google Cloud environment. The two primary requirements are:  
  
- Least-privilege access must always be enforced.  
- The DevOps team must access the necessary resources only for the duration of the deployment issue.  
  
How should access be granted according to Google-recommended best practices?

options.text: Assign the Project Viewer Identity and Access Management (IAM) role to the DevOps team.
Create a custom IAM role with limited list/view permissions, and assign it to the DevOps team.
Create a service account, and grant it the Project Owner IAM role. Give the Service Account User Role on this service account to the DevOps team.
Create a service account, and grant it limited list/view permissions. Give the Service Account User Role on this service account to the DevOps team.

questions.explanation:
A dedicated service account with only the necessary list/view permissions limits the effective permissions available during an investigation. Allowing the DevOps team to use that service account avoids assigning broader resource permissions directly to the team, whereas Project Owner and standing project-level viewer/custom-role assignments either exceed the required privilege or do not limit access to the incident period. Google Cloud recommends limiting service-account privileges and avoiding user impersonation of more-privileged service accounts.

**Learn more:** [Best practices for using service accounts securely](https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/best-practices-service-accounts) · [Use IAM securely](https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/using-iam-securely)

You are part of your company’s security team. You have been asked to reduce the external attack surface of your Linux bastion host by removing every public IP address. Site Reliability Engineers (SREs) need to reach the bastion host from public locations so they can access the internal VPC while off-site. How should you provide this access?

options.text: Implement Cloud VPN for the region where the bastion host lives.
Implement OS Login with 2-step verification for the bastion host.
Implement Identity-Aware Proxy TCP forwarding for the bastion host.
Implement Google Cloud Armor in front of the bastion host.

questions.explanation:
Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) TCP forwarding creates an encrypted, IAM-controlled tunnel for administrative services such as SSH to a VM’s internal IP address. It allows authorized SREs to access the bastion from the public internet without assigning the bastion a public, routable IP address.

**Learn more:** [Use IAP for TCP forwarding](https://docs.cloud.google.com/iap/docs/using-tcp-forwarding) · [TCP forwarding overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/iap/docs/tcp-forwarding-overview)

Your organization operates a workload regulated by European laws. You must prevent resources from being created outside the EU for this particular workload. You need an effective way to implement this security control without disrupting the other global applications. What should you do?

options.text: Create a Cloud Function triggered at asset creation that detects and deletes resources outside of the EU.
Create all your workload’s assets in a regional subnet in the EU in one project or folder.
Segment your workload in the EU in one project or folder by using VPC Service Controls.
Implement an organization policy that only allows the EU as the location for your workload’s project or folder.

questions.explanation:
An Organization Policy using the resource locations constraint can restrict where supported resources may be newly created. Applying it to the workload’s project or folder and allowing only EU locations scopes the preventive control to that workload, leaving other applications outside that resource-hierarchy branch unaffected.

**Learn more:** [Restrict resource locations](https://cloud.google.com/organization-policy/restrict-locations)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are auditing every Google Cloud resource in the production project and need to identify all principals that can modify firewall rules.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Use Policy Analyzer to query the permissions compute.firewalls.get or compute.firewalls.list.
Use Firewall Insights to understand your firewall rules usage patterns.
Reference the Security Health Analytics – Firewall Vulnerability Findings in the Security Command Center.
Use Policy Analyzer to query the permissions compute.firewalls.create or compute.firewalls.update or compute.firewalls.delete.

questions.explanation:
Policy Analyzer can query which principals have specified IAM permissions on resources. VPC firewall-rule changes require `compute.firewalls.create`, `compute.firewalls.update`, or `compute.firewalls.delete`; `compute.firewalls.get` and `compute.firewalls.list` provide only read access.

**Learn more:** [Policy Analyzer for allow policies](https://cloud.google.com/policy-intelligence/docs/policy-analyzer-overview) · [VPC firewall rules](https://cloud.google.com/firewall/docs/firewalls)

questions.question: lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You must implement an encryption-at-rest strategy that reduces key-management complexity for non-sensitive data and protects sensitive data, while retaining flexibility to control key residency and the rotation schedule. FIPS 140-2 L1 compliance is required for every data type. What should you do?

options.text: Encrypt non-sensitive data and sensitive data with Cloud External Key Manager.
Encrypt non-sensitive data and sensitive data with Cloud Key Management Service
Encrypt non-sensitive data with Google default encryption, and encrypt sensitive data with Cloud External Key Manager.
Encrypt non-sensitive data with Google default encryption, and encrypt sensitive data with Cloud Key Management Service.

questions.explanation:
Google default encryption automatically protects stored data with Google-managed keys, minimizing operational key management and using FIPS 140-2 Level 1-validated cryptography. Cloud Key Management Service customer-managed keys allow control of key location and rotation schedules, meeting the control requirements for sensitive data while providing FIPS 140-2 Level 1 validation.

**Learn more:** [Default encryption at rest](https://docs.cloud.google.com/docs/security/encryption/default-encryption) · [Cloud Key Management Service overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/kms/docs/key-management-service)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You must implement an encryption-at-rest strategy that protects sensitive data while reducing key-management complexity for non-sensitive data. Your solution must meet these requirements:  
  
- Schedule key rotation for sensitive data.  
- Control the region in which encryption keys for sensitive data are stored.  
- Minimize latency when accessing encryption keys for both sensitive and non-sensitive data.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Encrypt non-sensitive data and sensitive data with Cloud External Key Manager.
Encrypt non-sensitive data and sensitive data with Cloud Key Management Service.
Encrypt non-sensitive data with Google default encryption, and encrypt sensitive data with Cloud External Key Manager.
Encrypt non-sensitive data with Google default encryption, and encrypt sensitive data with Cloud Key Management Service.

questions.explanation:
Google default encryption protects non-sensitive data without requiring customer-managed key administration. Cloud KMS lets you create keys in a selected Cloud KMS location and configure automatic rotation schedules for symmetric encryption keys. Cloud EKM requires communication with an external key manager, for which Google documents geographic-latency and connectivity considerations; it is therefore less suitable when minimizing key-access latency is required.

**Learn more:** [Cloud KMS key rotation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/kms/docs/key-rotation) · [Create a Cloud KMS key](https://docs.cloud.google.com/kms/docs/create-key)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You are assisting a client that intends to migrate its data to Google Cloud. You must recommend an encryption service to manage its encrypted keys. The requirements are:  
  
- The master key must rotate at least once every 45 days.  
- The solution that stores the master key must be validated at FIPS 140-2 Level 3.  
- For redundancy, the master key must be stored across multiple regions in the US.  
  
Which solution satisfies these requirements?

options.text: Customer-managed encryption keys with Cloud Key Management Service
Customer-managed encryption keys with Cloud HSM
Customer-supplied encryption keys
Google-managed encryption keys

questions.explanation:
Customer-managed encryption keys with Cloud HSM use FIPS 140-2 Level 3 validated hardware security modules. Cloud KMS provides customer-controlled automatic rotation schedules for HSM-backed symmetric keys, including a 45-day schedule. Cloud HSM keys can be created in a U.S. multi-region, whose key material is stored in multiple regional data centers for redundancy.

**Learn more:** [Cloud HSM](https://docs.cloud.google.com/kms/docs/hsm?hl=en) · [Cloud KMS locations](https://docs.cloud.google.com/kms/docs/locations)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],For compliance reporting, the internal audit department requires a list of virtual machines (VMs) with critical operating system (OS) security updates available but not installed. You must provide this list every six months and want to complete the task quickly.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: Run a Security Command Center security scan on all VMs to extract a list of VMs with critical OS vulnerabilities every six months.
Run a gcloud CLI command from the Command Line Interface (CLI) to extract the VM's OS version information every six months.
Ensure that the Cloud Logging agent is installed on all VMs, and extract the OS last update log date every six months.
Ensure the OS Config agent is installed on all VMs and extract the patch status dashboard every six months.

questions.explanation:
VM Manager’s Patch dashboard provides fleet-wide patch-compliance information. Its **Critical** category identifies VMs that have critical updates available; VMs must have the OS Config agent installed and OS inventory management enabled to appear in the dashboard.

**Learn more:** [About Patch | VM Manager | Google Cloud Documentation](https://cloud.google.com/compute/vm-manager/docs/patch)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],You manage network traffic for a folder in your Google Cloud environment. The folder contains multiple projects and Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) networks. You need to enforce, at the folder level, that egress connections are limited to IP range `10.58.5.0/24` and originate only from the VPC network `dev-vpc`. You want to minimize implementation and maintenance effort.  
  
What should you do?

options.text: 1. Leave the network configuration of the VMs in scope unchanged.2. Create a new project including a new VPC network “new-vpc”.3. Deploy a network appliance in “new-vpc” to filter access requests and only allow egress connections from “dev-vpc” to 10.58.5.0/24.
1. Leave the network configuration of the VMs in scope unchanged.2. Enable Cloud NAT for “dev-vpc” and restrict the target range in Cloud NAT to 10.58.5.0/24.

1. Attach external IP addresses to the VMs in scope.2. Define and apply a hierarchical firewall policy on folder level to deny all egress connections and to allow egress to IP range 10.58.5.0/24 from network dev-vpc.
1. Attach external IP addresses to the VMs in scope.2. Configure a VPC Firewall rule in “dev-vpc” that allows egress connectivity to IP range 10.58.5.0/24 for all source addresses in this network.

questions.explanation:
Hierarchical firewall policies can be associated with a folder and apply to VPC networks in projects beneath that folder. A higher-priority egress allow rule targeted to `dev-vpc` for destination `10.58.5.0/24`, followed by a lower-priority deny-all egress rule, permits only the required traffic and blocks egress from every other VPC network in the folder.

**Learn more:** [Configure a hierarchical firewall policy to allow egress traffic from a specific VPC network](https://docs.cloud.google.com/firewall/docs/quickstarts/configure-hfwpolicy-allow-egress-vpc) · [Hierarchical firewall policies](https://docs.cloud.google.com/firewall/docs/firewall-policies)
